comments: Take the class! It is very well designed and Lucas is a great classroom discussion facilitator. All the prep work felt very intentional and never felt like the assignments were busy work. The Electricity Strategy Game was a helpful simulation for getting acquainted with the market dynamics of real energy markets. The daily indicators were another highlight of the class that allowed me to learn a truly diverse range of topics from my peers. I love this feature of the class because it added variety and context to the topics we covered. One of the most valuable and applicable classes I've taken at Haas.

sections.goodFor: Anyone wanting CFO-level financial decision-making - profitability, financing decisions, valuation. Pivots into finance, consultants, GMs. Many say it should be core. Pick a good team.
sections.notFor: Students with no finance background and only passive interest. Several felt behind in a cohort full of banking backgrounds; one says don't take it unless ready for 5+ hrs/week staying afloat.
sections.workloadNote: One graded case per week worked in groups, ~5+ hours each; readings are light. Heavy but repeatedly described as never busy work, with concepts revisited every few classes.
sections.gradingBasis: Weekly group cases graded pass/fail on effort (called flexible), plus a final students expect to be conceptual, not calculation-based.
sections.redFlags: Two criticize the case format: you self-teach the case (often with AI), then re-walk it in class, adding little if you already know finance. Several say non-finance students find it frustrating.
sections.quote: Be warned that this class is a LOT of work: we had one case a week (to be worked on in groups) and each case took ~5+ hours.
comments: Yes if you're interested in finance. If not, it can get a bit heavy. Still good topics to know and I find myself reading the news and picking up on aspects I learned. Plus gustavo makes it interesting with discussions of the news each week. Yes
Yes! Great engaging class where you will learn the tools for a career in finance
Yes. As someone pivoting into finance, I found this class super helpful in giving me a sense of the tools used and needed in finance!
Hard class but you'll learn a lot!
Yes - this is a must-take class during MBA

I was very excited to take this class and am unfortunately disappointed. Coming in with some finance background, I do not think I am walking away with new skills. The case structure is extremely ineffective. You teach yourself how to go through a case using AI, then go to class and walk through the case that you already went through, which rarely adds value.

Such a well-organized course, that establishes from the beginning what you are expected to learn and coherently builds knowledge week on and week out. Contents are reviewed every few classes, so as to solidify learning. Best course I have taken at Haas.
Yes! The cases are a lot of work, but you learn a ton, and Professor Manso is amazing. It's a heavy lift course, but it's worth taking if you have any interest in finance.

Yes!! This should be a core requirement for the MBA. Super important concepts and tools are embedded that are relevant across most scales of business, even outside of corporations. Prof Manso is one of my favorite professors I've had at Haas.

He's one of the most academically brilliant yet humble professors I have ever met. He truly shines out in what he does and makes the classes so engaging. He's one of the best at Haas and it's been a privilege to be taught by him! I enthusiastically recommend taking this class by Prof Gustavo
Prof Manso is awesome and this course was super helpful. As someone coming from a non-business background I feel way more confident making investment decisions now. Highly recommend!
I would but I would say that it is a heavy lift and that you get what you put into it.

Yes, this class has been my favorite class at Haas so far. Prof Manso is really good at taking complex ideas and breaking them down so they are easier to understand. The class may feel a little overwhelming at first, but it gets better with time and has been a very rewarding course for me. I highly recommend everyone at Haas to take this class. Professor Manso is very skilled at breaking down complex topics into understandable components. The way he integrated current news stories into the cases/lectures added very helpful context. Overall, he's a very engaging professor who makes a challenging topic enjoyable to learn!

Absolutely recommend! Learned more about how to think like a CFO (tools, strategies) than any other Haas class so far. Probably should be required in Core. Pick a great team, do the cases, and it will be the best class you take. Yes, for someone who never had any understanding of corporate finance or finance before, this class was compact enough to give me a perspective of corporate finance that will able to support my career later in finance sector The most worth course I have taken so far. I'm not even interested in a finance career but it doesn't matter because I now understand what finance is about for a company and what are the challenges that a CFO faces. It taught me to read the news better, to be better at talking about financial challenges and design strategy to attack/defend my company based on the nature of the finances

This is a must-take class at Haas, and for me it should be part of the core. The course focuses on the finance applications that are relevant in a corporate context (especially how to make stronger financial decisions - if you want to be a CFO, board member or any c-level those are important concepts). Professor Manso is excellent- his teaching style is clear, the course is very well organized, and the overall design works great. That said, it is definitely not a low- lift class, since it includes weekly cases and requires preparation. Still, it is absolutely worth it.
10/10 would recommend. It was structured with concepts, slides, readings all clearly laid out. Workload was on the heavier side but never busy work. I learned a lot!
Yes, rigorous and challenging but probably good for business students
Yes, I would highly recommend this course to other students - this was the best Haas class that I took by far, and will be very useful going forward even if I don't go into finance

As someone who was truly dreading this course, Gustavo made it both approachable and enjoyable. He clearly takes such joy in teaching and it really shines through in the way he approaches his lectures and discussions. He is one of the few professors I've had that fully engages with student responses to his questions without shooting people down when they're wrong, leading to a very comfortable environment. The only time he cold calls is to describe the case which in theory everyone should have read and doesn't require any additional knowledge. And he's always open to reviewing concepts or taking a step back to re-explain things.
Absolutely. This is one of the best courses I've taken at haas so far. I thought finance was accounting, now I know that it's strategy.
Yes. 10000000% yes. Don't think about it - just do it!
100%. We need to know finance

Gustavo is a strong classroom instructor and facilitator who creates a safe environment for students to learn about a complex and nuanced topic. I appreciated the arc of the course and how he laid out the journey repeatedly so that students knew what to expect and what we were building toward. The class is a lot of work and I didn't always understand what was going on, but I learned a great deal thoroughout the semester that helped me make more sense of the world around me and of the concepts we learn about in other courses.
Yes. Highly recommended
Yes if they are interested in finance.
Yes, builds nicely on the intro to finance core class and is good to understand no matter what you go out into the world and do post business school

Gustavo is super knowledgeable and a really engaging teacher. He made the topics interesting and relevant to the real world. I loved that he would bring in props and incorporate humor in his lectures as well. It was a great experience! I highly recommend this class.:)

Absolutely - if one wants to strengthen not only their modeling skills but their understanding of finance, this class is one of the most worthwhile at Haas. It does come with a lot of work on weekly basis but it is most definitely a net positive.
Absolutely. Most i've learned in a class so far. Very effective use of cases and practical applications to teach valuable lessons
This class is a lot of work! It's worthwhile, but don't underestimate the workload. Gustavo is a great professor. Yes absolutely. Great intro to broader finance

I would recommend this class! It goes deeper than core finance and allows you to apply each concept through cases. The grading of cases is very flexible so while it's a lot of work you don't have to worry about your grades. Gustavo is a very good professor. If you don't have a finance background, this class will be incredibly frustrating and discouraging at times. The class tends to have a lot of people with finance and banking backgrounds. I often felt behind. However the GSIs are very helpful and I feel like I have a strong grasp on finance topics that will set me up for my next career. The class discussions about news were sometimes more interesting than others. This class leans heavily on finance enthusiasts. Be aware that having a passive interest in finance might find this class dry at times.

Gustavo is a great and kind instructor, but my recommendation depends on your background / discipline. If you have a finance background or can commit to attending office hours/ limiting your AI use, this is a great and practical class. If you have a limited finance background, then this case format mostly requires that you teach yourself concepts you may have never heard of or faintly remember from core finance and apply to it a case. The following class, Gustavo does go over the case and concepts in depth which is helpful but can feel frustrating if you relied on AI to help you do the case and didn't really internalize the concepts. Grading of cases is based on effort which is great and the final seems like its going to be more conceptual questions rather than any actual calculations which is a huge relief. A Haas must-take class for everyone. This really should be called Strategic Finance as it is mainly a case-based class discussing the strategic implications of CFO decisions. The content is extremely interesting and applied to recent news. Gustavo is one of the best professors here, he explains super clearly and has a great sense of humor for what would be otherwise thought of as a dry subject.

Some other people may comment that the weekly cases were time intensive, but I think it's in line with other classes - the reading is light and the cases are done in groups on a pass/fail basis so no need to kill yourself over getting the right answer (and you won't - I don't think anyone gets the same answer as the professor due to the complexity of the cases).
Yes. It's a good intro to the heavier categories of finance.

This is the best class I've taken at Haas. In some ways I just wish I took it earlier (but also the course load is no joke so I'm glad I took it during a semester I didn't have much else going on). I think it is the most useful and applicable course for anyone looking to strengthen their finance intuition.
You absolutely should not take this class unless you have a background in finance and/or are excited at the prospect of spending 5+ hours a week staying afloat

I would definitely recommend this course to anyone looking to better understand corporate finance tools such as understanding profitability, financing decisions, and valuation. Be warned that this class is a LOT of work: we had one case a week (to be worked on in groups) and each case took ~5+ hours. That being said, the effort is worth it if you want to learn about finance. Professor Manso is awesome and does a great job of breaking down the concepts. As someone with very little prior finance knowledge, I feel way more equipped for my future consulting career! Yes! Learned a lot

sections.goodFor: Every MBA, especially anyone with little professional negotiation experience who wants repeated low-stakes simulation practice and self-diagnosis.
sections.notFor: No student named a group who should avoid it; the only friction mentioned is the 3-hour (8am) block.
sections.workloadNote: Light outside class - one student notes 'there wasn't a ton of work outside of class time and the prep was all work that actually made a difference for negotiating'.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; in-class negotiation simulations and prep are the visible work.
sections.quote: The class teaches many fundamental business skills and more importantly provides a lab for simulated practice of negotiation to understand your strengths and address your weaknesses.
comments: Absolutely, one of the most useful and engaging classes at Haas, even if you think you already known how to negotiate. It's such a well constructed course with applications that go far beyond sales or procurement, and I can highly recommend Drew!

Yes, I would certainly recommend for anyone trying to sharpen their negotiation skills and have the ability to practice real world scenarios in a low stakes enviroment. Drew is engaging and great professor.
definitely recommend, you can polish your negotiation skills by doing lots of simulations
I would absolutely recommend this course to a fellow student!
YES Drew is awesome and this course is great for anyone who has never taken a negotiations course before. Yes, your MBA will not be complete without this. Must take!
Must take course for all MBA students
definitely, very introspective and a lot of tools to take away and use in the future
Yes I would. The class teaches many fundamental business skills and more importantly provides a lab for simulated practice of negotiation to understand your strengths and address your weaknesses.
Yes! Drew is a great explainer and helps you see what you need to know about the material without bogging you down in details, unless you'd like to!
Absolutely! One of my favorite courses I've taken at Haas. Very actionable and a great way to practice skills that will be useful throughout your career and personal life.
Absolutely
Yes, great instructor and class. Coming from a background with minimal professional negotiation experience, I found this to be an excellent class
Yes, this was one of the most impactful courses I've had at Haas as it equips you with strategies you can use to employ in your professional and personal life immediately.
Definitely. Great class and really fun.

Yes - learned effective negotiation strategies that are widely applicable in professional and personal life Yes this is a must take class in the MBA. 100% would say people should take this and learn more about themselves, their negotiation style and how to improve.
Yes, very useful
Yes!

Drew is fantastic! Three hours is a really long time and I think he managed the class well and negotiating in class helped break it up. I appreciated that there wasn't a ton of work outside of class time and the prep was all work that actually made a difference for negotiating. It was really good practice for me to get more comfortable and think about what is effective for me and not.

Yes, one of my favorite classes and I really enjoyed the opportunity to practice negotiating so much. I think I've improved a lot over the course and I'm excited to take these skills with me into the workforce.
Yes, one of the most useful courses I've taken at Haas. I used to be really insecure about my negotiation skills and now I know anything is learnable
Yes instructor is very prepared for lectures
Yes, it is the most valuable course ive done and very interactive
Yes
Absolutely! You'll learn so much and it's a fun class. So useful

Absolutely, do not graduate from the MBA without this class -- it is a key skill for life! Drew is an excellent professor with great content and teaching style (almost makes an 8 am class not a pain):)

sections.goodFor: Anyone wanting repeated live negotiation reps — several recommend taking it in year one for job-hunt confidence. Useful for team dynamics beyond formal negotiation.
sections.notFor: Very little criticism. One student notes takeaways 'weren't completely concrete'; another suggests it lands better with some work experience behind you.
sections.workloadNote: 'There is some outside work but nothing exhaustive.' The bulk of the work is in class: prepping and running a negotiation, then debriefing it the same session.
sections.gradingBasis: Case-based in-class negotiations/role plays and debriefs; grade weights not discussed.
sections.quote: The real world negotiation practice was invaluable and I thought the way the negotiation concepts were presented in class were straightforward and easy to understand.
comments: Yes!
I think you can improve a lot of personal skills, or at least put them into practice.
YES
Yes, lots of useful skills

Yes, would recommend, great skill to have, very effective teaching method and style, entertaining and engaging class. Yes absolutely. I have been recommending this course since the 2nd week to everyone

Yes- I think this course is important during the MBA. The role play experience is good for boosting confidence. I'd recommend taking the course in first year as it can give you confidence with your peers/job hunt.
Yes

Yes, I would recommend it - great hands on practice and simulation. Professor Jacoby Senghor was great, very engaging. Overall the biggest benefit was practicing reps of negotiations to get more comfortable. Takeaways weren't completely concrete for me, but I might need to review the materials.
YES!!! This is one of the most hands on courses ive taken during my program
Yes 100%
I'd definitely recommend this course. It's case-based with a lot of interactions with classmates. There is some outside work but nothing exhaustive.

This was one of the most helpful classes I've taken at Haas. I absolutely loved how Drew structured the class - prepping for and conducting a negotiation during the class, while de-briefing and going over the negotiation afterwards. Drew clearly cares a lot about this class, and their passion is infectious. I felt like they genuinely wanted their students to do well and learn the material, and that made me want to be a better student as well
Yes! This is one of the best classes you can do at Haas
Very fun and valuable for all career.

Yes! I learned a good amount, it's useful to practice negotiations throughout the class, and fun to interact with classmates in this manner.
Yes

I would recommend this instructor and course!! He is so good at teaching as mentioned earlier and he made a 3 hr class breeze by. Yes - it made me have really uncomfortable conversations and get better at holding my ground while remaining cordial during negotiations

I would absolutely recommend both the instructor and the course. I have heard from classmates who previously enrolled in this class a couple of years ago, and still use the same approaches taught in this syllabus. I would 100% recommend this course to other students; it's a great course and a great skill to learn.
Yes, I would 100% recommend both the professor and the course. Negotiation is a fundamental skill for professional life, and the professor does a great job teaching it in an effective way.
Yes. Very practical class. For those with little negotiation experience is a must.
Yes, permit you to learn both about negotiation toolkit, practice it and learning about you as a negotiator I would recommend the course

sections.goodFor: Anyone curious about VC or impact investing, beginner or experienced - you effectively do an associate's job for a semester and build a founder/Haas network; one landed an internship from it.
sections.notFor: Students who can't commit real time, or who want a lecture-structured class - it is mostly independent learning and your experience depends on a randomly assigned team.
sections.workloadNote: Short structured crash course in new venture finance up front, then roughly three months of real VC work - founder calls, sourcing, due diligence - largely independent and team-driven.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; work is team due diligence on real startups plus a brief front-end frameworks module. Grading itself is never discussed.
sections.redFlags: Two students flag that a good part of the experience depends on your randomly assigned group, and stress the real time commitment and heavy independent learning. No other complaints in 23 comments.
sections.quote: Unfortunately, good part of the class experience depends on your group and that is random, but if you have a neutral or good group and you're invested in the class, you'll learn a lot in practice.
comments: Absolutely! I keep telling everyone this is my MBA capstone, because it brings together everything I've learned in the MBA. I feel like I've actually gotten VC experience and have built up a pretty cool network of Haasies and founders Yes!
Absolutely. If you are even slightly curious about investing and impact investing, this class is great for intro as well as for experienced professionals.
Yes. Really knowledgeable professor.

Yes with the caveat it does depend on the team you get placed with, which is selected for you. This course is great because it gives real exposure and practice to startups, business models and funding. I got so much more out of this than a lecture and appreciate the hands on learning

Absolutely, take this class if you want to get a real experience of what it is like to be a venture capitalist. yes, 1000%. super practical crash course in new venture finance followed by a real application of VC investing for 3 months. one of the best semesters I've had at Haas.
YES - one of the best applied innovation classes I've taken! I took this and IBD and got great takeaways from both - the more real life application we can do in the classroom the better!
Yes, if you are a beginner in this space.

For anyone interested in VC, social impact, or impact investing, this is a must-take class! It's a lot of independent learning but I've learned more in this semester than I have in most other classes. If you're on the fence, take it! Absolutely. I took this class because I was curious about impact VC. I got that and so much more out of this class. I really owe my future career aspirations to this class.

Highly recommend. This was one of the most impactful courses to truly understanding the work of a VC investor. I learned a lot &, more importantly, had the chance to put my learnings into practice with numerous calls with startups Great class and one of the best I've taken at Haas.

YES, as long as you're committed to spending a solid time on it. Unfortunately, good part of the class experience depends on your group and that is random, but if you have a neutral or good group and you're invested in the class, you'll learn a lot in practice. Jeep and Adair are inspiring, knowledgeable and extremely accessible. One of my favorite classes!

I really learned a lot from this course - this course really teaches you how to be VC. I talked with many inspiring founders and learned a ton about the industry. There is a lot of work especially team work but the more time you spend the more rewarding it is.
Absolutely - best class I've taken.
Yes
If you are interested in how the VC due diligence process works from either the founder or the VC persepective, this course is awesome!

I would absolutely recommend this course! This was my favorite class at Haas. I learned a lot about impact investing. Take this if you're curious what impact investing is like. You do the job for a few months and can see if it's for you. This experience also helped me land an internship in the space.
Yes., Great course to take if you are interested in learning more about how venture capital works and being able to see it happen in action.
Yes,I've recommended the class to everyone who asked for what class to take in Spring

Absolutely. This class was very informative and took us through the journey of a what an associate working VC might do over the course of their company search. I liked that there was a brief structured portion of the class where we learned about frameworks and other basic industry knowledge, and that we had plenty of time for application in the real world.
This is the best course at Haas! You get to be an actual VC! Take this course even if you don't want to do VC, its just really good experience!!!

sections.goodFor: Students with no prior venture experience who want a real VC rep - sourcing deals, meeting founders, running diligence, pitching. Noted as flexible/remote-friendly for EWMBA after the first few weeks.
sections.notFor: People who already worked in venture (one says take a different Applied Innovation class), anyone not genuinely interested (it becomes a lot of work), and those expecting a real impact focus.
sections.workloadNote: Not quantified but repeatedly called a heavy lift; about half the course is lab time. Load is elastic - meet minimum assignment requirements, or sink endless hours into sourcing and diligence.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; minimum assignment requirements plus sourcing, due diligence and pitch deliverables
sections.redFlags: 2 students say the 'Impact' name is a misnomer - the class de-emphasizes impact and focuses on market-rate returns. Workload is team-dependent, and the $75k check size makes sourcing hard.
sections.quote: Will add that the "Impact" naming is a bit of a misnomer -- from day 1, the class de-emphasizes impact and focuses heavily on market-rate returns.
comments: Yes
Absolutely. I wish I was able to take it sooner (it bid out when I was a first year). One of the most practical classes I took at Haas.
Yes. I believe anyone interested in venture capital and financing young companies with high potential should take this course.
yes! so fun getting our hands dirty with sourcing and due diligence. I realize there's still a lot of quant concepts I don't fully understand, but perhaps that is the reality of the industry.

Yes -- both Jeep and Adair were phenomenal instructors, and I found the overall course to be worthwhile, especially if you are aspiring to be in VC or otherwise just exploring it as a potential pathway. You really do get to act as a VC for the course of the semester, so it's a great opportunity to see how you like it and build some experience. The workload can be what you make of it -- if you/your team want to go all in, you could spend endless time sourcing and screening deals, diligencing, etc; you can fulfill minimum assignment requirements with a lot less work, though, if you don't feel passionate about investing a ton of time.

Will add that the "Impact" naming is a bit of a misnomer -- from day 1, the class de-emphasizes impact and focuses heavily on market-rate returns. Be warned if you are primarily taking this for the "Impact" spin, and know that it's really just traditional VC with a hint of impact framing.

This is a great class if you want to experience being a VC with lower stakes than in the real world. It is a heavy lift class and you need to be prepared to spend a lot of time sourcing deals, meeting founders and doing due diligence on the companies. Your experience will be very team dependent so how much work you do also depends on how engaged your team is. The professors are phenomenal and are always very willing to help students throughout.
Yes would recommend
100%!! Really great class. Honestly just wish I took it earlier as it would have helped me a lot!!
Yes I do. There is no better way to connect with start-ups, than saying that we can invest in them. Also, helps understand what a good start up is.
Yes, great way to get your hands dirty and practice sourcing and evaluation.
Yes I'd recommend this class, you are thrown into the deep end but you learn how to be a VC in a very hands on way, so it's worth it

Yes! if you are interested in learning about what it is like to be a VC but also want to focus on impact investing, this is the course to take! you will learn so much about another world of VC but also, it was really neat to learn about all the differnt companies in the different sectors where impact is needed.

Yes, I would recommend as long as they are interested in VC and/or impact investing. It gives real life hands-on experience on sourcing, performing due diligence and pitching. However if you are not very interested, it will be a lot of work and you won't enjoy.

Yes I would highly recommend this class to anyone who is interested in early-stage technology or VC investing. Anyone who is dissuaded by the "impact" framing of the class should speak to a past student who will surely emphasize the practical learning from the class and the very professionally applicable nature of the content. If you're interested in the real VC experience, it's the class that you must take. Although the workload may be higher than in other classes, the hands-on experience as a VC and learning is truly something that you want to get out of your MBA program.
Strongly recommend - very good opportunity to think and evaluate as a VC
Yes, this is the most practical and fun course I've taken at Haas. Very much recommend for quality of instruction, for anyone interested in impact investing or VC

If you have never done anything in venture before, then I 100% recommend this class. It's exactly what you would get from a venture internship, and Adair and Jeep provide a safe space to explore and learn. They are open, direct, and honest. I greatly appreciated their feedback. If you have been in venture before, then I don't think you need to take this class. I would invest your time learning something new in another Applied Innovation class.

Adair is a seasoned educator. You can tell that she is passionate about teaching and she really tries to decrease the amount of busy work in class. Jeep is a great investor. She's got incredible stories about what she has invested in and really encourages individuals to find their own passions / areas of investment. Both professors give up a lot of time to help students enter the vc space and riff off of each other. This is the first VC class I've taken at Haas where it's not a "bro" culture dominated space. Would highly recommend if you're interested in VC and/or talking to entrepreneurs. I would definitely recommend the Haas Impact Fund for those who are looking for hands on VC experience. It's a really fun class because you are actively sourcing real deals, so you meet with founders and do due diligence with real financials and materials from early stage companies. For EWMBA students - you have to get to campus by 4pm for a few weeks in the beginning of the semester, but then the rest of the semester you don't need to go to campus because you're coordinating remotely with your team. So it's actually quite flexible which can be especially good for EWMBA students. Lastly, Jeep and Adair are fantastic professors - getting to learn from them is a privilege. Really cool course but be prepared to dedicate the time and effort. The 75k check size is a bit of a challenge so be prepared to build and use your networks to access deals and improve your sourcing funnel. Adair and Jeep are amazing and it's worth taking the course just to work with them. But I can't emphasize this enough - the course requires time and there aren't any shortcuts at the end of the day so make sure you know what you're signing up for. Absolutely! Great way to learn what it takes to be a VC and guided by supportive, sharp advisors who bring experience from the field.

I would recommend this experiential learning course to anyone who is interesting in gaining quick learning and hands- on experience in VC. The impact part of the course is also meaningful, but it does not take away from the VC-learning aspect of the course. You have to plan on having a lot of time to do out of class work. This is a time intensive projec- based course; similar in the vein of time commitment to clean tech to market etc. Make sure your schedule allows you the time you need to do the work; as long as this is well set up for you, the course and instructors will deliver an awesome learning experience.
I would definitely recommend Haas Impact Fund to a fellow student. The class's hands-on-experience and material created a learning experience unique in the program. I really enjoyed this class.

I'd recommend this course to the students who are prepping to get into VC. It's a great class to network with VCs and founders. I've learned a lot from professors, mentors, founders, and investors. There is a lot of self-study involved as well, since half of the course is lab time.
Take this class if you want to work on investing for a potential move into the field (or to learn about being an angel).

sections.goodFor: Current or aspiring managers wanting a concrete 1:1 coaching framework, better questioning skills, and lots of live practice — applicable to personal life too.
sections.notFor: Only caveat raised is format: full-day Sunday sessions are long. No substantive content criticism appeared in any comment.
sections.workloadNote: Manageable, compressed into two Sunday sessions. Class time is dominated by small-group coaching practice and feedback reps rather than lecture; 'the more you put into it, the more you'll get out.'
sections.gradingBasis: In-class coaching practice and participation; grading not discussed.
sections.quote: The class can be long on a sunday but workload is manageable, and the more you put into it, the more you'll get out of it.
comments: This class is good at honing in on coaching vs therapy. It's good for anyone who wants to ultimately lead an organization and work on their interpersonal skills. The class can be long on a sunday but workload is manageable, and the more you put into it, the more you'll get out of it.

Highly recommend this class. It was one of the most practical, applicable courses I've taken at Haas. And, while I usually struggle with the length of Sunday classes, the amount of small group engagement and practice made the class length make sense to me
I definitely recommend. This is one of my favorite course by far. I have learned so much not only about coaching but also my life in just two Sundays.
Yes, must take. Some of the few very useful classes for your personal and professional life.
Yes because 1:1 coaching is important for managers
Would HIGHLY recommend this course and these instructors. one of my favorite Haas classes! So useful and will leverage these frameworks for the rest of my career. (and personal life!)

Yes, I would recommend to anyone who want to develop skills in coaching. The hands on practice was very effective. Great course for people who love to help unleash the potential in others! Helps you think about what it means to be a coach and how to be coached better as well.

This was a great course to learn how to coach without imposing your views on others and engaging empathetically and focusing on the outcome for your coach-ee. There is tons of practice to get good at the skill with enough flexibility for you to practice out your own style. Ultimately I would recommend this class to anyone looking to learn how to ask better questions and bring a meaningful impact to those you work and connect with.
Yes, it's very helpful to grow as a leader to understand coaching. The framework used was highly effective and something ill use the rest of my career

I would definitely recommend this course if you want to practice coaching. I thought I knew what being a good coach looked like before and I realized it was much harder than expected, so now I feel a lot more prepared to be a coach Yes
Yes, think coaching is a very important skill to learn and understand

Yes because it allows for the tip of the iceberg to be encountered around social issues, but be prepared and wary for the class to be extremely capitalistic without much data/room for counterarguments. When issues and questioning of the status quo came up, many times, the instructors didn't have the answers or relied on conceptual concepts. Math or data isn't used much in this class to back up arguments rather than descriptive statistics. This class allows someone to be creative around solving social issues, but at its underlying core, the course doesn't answer the crucial answer in its entirety of how do you solve or combat social issues. The course feels that it helps one brainstorm bandaid business oriented solutions without exploring issues at its core and how to truly combat it. Moreover, the course makes a lot of excuses for the pitfalls of capitalism and expects it to be passed off. For example, when discussing compensation structures and how they're centered around the course's impact triangle concept, it became dicey with no solutions offered. One thing to point out is that readings really push the capitalist perspective to social issues rather than diverse issues, particularly in overworking workers and labor by stretching them thin for value. Burnout is accepted and normalized. Another example would be each business leader that came in already operated with mindsets that they're doing their best without much emphasis on how they're solving the underlying root causes of each problem. All in all, the course allows for a student to be challenged and explore different models out there and it's good to address the overlaying present issues, but not great at addressing underlying issues and deriving a model from there. Case studies, videos, and resources are great!

These are gems who will guide you on your journey as a social entrepreneur. Yes! I've been in the social impact space (across nonprofit, foundaiton and corporate) for 10 years and havent been formally trained in some of these topics so being grounded in that was very applicable and relevant for me than other business classes. sections.goodFor: Juniors/seniors and anyone earning income; repeatedly recommended by first-gen and low-income students, internationals staying in the US, and total finance novices.
sections.notFor: Freshmen and students who have never earned income - the retirement/tax/insurance focus feels irrelevant; anyone already financially literate will find it basic.
sections.workloadNote: Consistently light: 2 hours of class weekly, supplemental videos, quizzes, a 3-stage budgeting assignment, midterm and final. Don't fall behind on the videos.
sections.gradingBasis: Quizzes and exams pulling specific questions from the supplemental videos, plus assignments; attendance is enforced and drew a complaint.

Definitely take this class. The community is awesome, and getting three units of credit to work on your own startup, with real time and resources to build momentum, is a pretty rare opportunity. The class also gives you credits for Lovable, AWS, Claude Pro, and other tools, which makes a real difference when you're building.

Compared to programs like Lean Launch Pad, which lean heavily on customer interviews alone with a tight weekly cadence of identical deliverables for every team, this is much more flexible. You'll still do customer discovery, but you'll also have the structure to leverage the newest AI tools and actually ship in parallel. Different startups can be at different stages — you can pivot, break up with your team and join a new one, start over, and run customer discovery and building in parallel. This structure also reflects how products are actually getting built today. Software is so much cheaper to ship now, so customer discovery and building can happen in parallel, not in the old waterfall sequence of research-then-build. The class mirrors how real startups operate, which makes the experience much more applicable to the real world. Progress is defined in terms of what's actually moving the needle for your team's specific venture, not busywork deliverables. It feels like a real incubator, not a academic checklist.

How the class is structured: you're making real progress every week. Class sessions usually open with an hour topic overview from the professors, followed by a guest speaker, and then dedicated mentoring time where you can get advice from the week's in person mentors and collaborate with teammates and other peers on whatever challenges you're working through. The mentor program is a real highlight. There's a deep roster of mentors brought in from a wide range of backgrounds and industries, and you have choice in who you work with. Combined with the peer collaboration in class, the community feels built in and there to support everyone.

Set your expectations going in: if you're looking for a tightly structured curriculum with a lot of rigorous frameworks, this may not be that. But if you come in thinking of it as a great incubator community led by Omri (who's an exceptional teacher and infuses life lessons alongside entrepreneurship lesson) you'll get a ton out of it. He's beloved for good reason. One signal of how inspiring this community is: about 20 of the 27 teams from this cohort are continuing their ventures past the end of the class. That speaks for itself. Heads up that it's a lot of work, plan for it to take meaningful time and energy. But if you're game for that, you'll learn a ton.

Even if you're not sure entrepreneurship is your long-term path, this class is still worth taking. With AI, the lines between PM, engineer, designer, and user researcher are collapsing, we may not even have separate roles for much longer, just "builders." This class is one of the best opportunities at Haas to practice being an "AI builder", wearing all those hats at once. You'll do real customer research, real building, and real iteration alongside teammates with different perspectives, with your ideas challenged by real customers. The broader skills: flexible thinking, customer empathy, the ability to pivot and learn from your learnings, humility, the willingness to try different creative approaches, are applicable far beyond entrepreneurship. I'd recommend this for anyone with curiosity about AI, entrepreneurship, product, or even just what it's like to spend a semester working with a team on a creative project. I highly recommend taking this class because it gives you the opportunity to actually build a product and learn through practice. However, I suggest that students come in with a validated idea (for example, already having done 20–30 customer interviews); otherwise, you may end up spending half of the course on customer discovery, while teams that start with a concrete idea can use the time to build and iterate on their product. I would even recommend taking Lean Launchpad, which focuses heavily on customer discovery, before this class so that you can get the most benefit from the experience.

Yes! Very practical and relevant course.
