Yes. I found it to be a perfect class to learn about difficult topics and situations that you might not learn otherwise. The workload is light but just enough to make you think a lot about what you would do in a real situation.

If you are interested about supply chain in the big tech compagny yes. Both the course and the guest speaker will be really useful for you. If Supply chain is not your main focus I will not recommend this course.

I enjoyed this class! I took it for the credit towards the Sustainable Business certificate and thought it would be boring, but they kept the class interesting with a variety of topics and approaches.
I would absolutely recommend this course to anyone interested in learning more about supply chain and how

companies have been thoughtful about creating a responsible and sustainable supply chain, especially on a larger scale. There were many relevant cases and it was very eye-opening to learn about how companies operate and what the trade-offs are.

I would definitely recommend this class! It's been the most interesting class I have taken at Haas so far. The professors balance each other out and do a good job of managing classroom discussions. The class as a whole is a good balance of case review + discussion and guest speakers who may have been involved in the case directly. Definitely recommend to anyone who is interested in supply chain crises, sustainable supply chains, and human rights. Yes, a great overview of supply chain, responsible methods, and excellent industry guest speakers
Yes - Interesting subject matter, changed my perspective. Course is pretty light after the first few weeks and you'll get more out of it if you are interested in supply chain / ops roles.

100% would recommend this course. Whether you are someone looking to get into supply chain sustainability or responsibility, or you're a skeptic to the idea these words have any place in a business environment you should take this class. It is well-taught and well-backed. I don't think I want to go into supply chain after this class, but it was something that I certainly learned along the way. This was possibly my favorite class of my second year.

Yes! Hans done one of my favorite classes at Haas. The lectures are fun, engaging, and you learn a lot about how complex supply chains are. The instructors are super intentional and care about student input so I'm sure the class will be even better next year!

sections.goodFor: Students who want a discussion space on race where they feel heard; framed as preparation for building equitable, bias-aware workplaces as future managers.
sections.notFor: Not addressed - with only 2 comments there is no evidence about who should avoid it.
sections.workloadNote: Thin evidence: only 2 comments, neither discusses workload, assignments or grading.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear
sections.quote: Yes for sure, it's a great class where you are heard and also learn a lot
comments: Yes for sure, it's a great class where you are heard and also learn a lot

I will 100% recommend this instructor and course. In fact, I wish this was a core class. The learnings in this course have a direct impact on our lives. And as future managers and business leaders at Haas it is necessary to equip ourselves with the learnings from this class so that we can help create a more equitable, fair and bias free work environment. Yes! Please everyone take this class it's so wonderful and I learned a lot

rows.title: Data-Driven Presentations: Making the Business Case
Strategically Managing Healthcare Policy - Washington Campus

sections.goodFor: Students curious about how health policy is actually made, influenced and interpreted in Washington DC — works even without a healthcare background.
sections.notFor: No criticism raised in the three comments; too thin to identify who should avoid it.
sections.workloadNote: Very thin evidence — only 3 comments, none of which mention workload, assignments or hours.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear
sections.quote: I would absolutely recommend this course for anyone who wants to know 'how the sausage is made' with regards to how policies are instigated, influenced and interpreted
comments: Yes, even if you may not have a health background, the course has been very interesting and helpful to understand the ever changing health policy landscape.

Kim MacPherson is amazing! She is thoughtful, expansive in her knowledge and knows how to push our thinking boundaries in a way that is respectful and effective. She knows enough about most major healthcare topics and does an excellent job of connecting dots and bringing in the MBA perspective.

I would absolutely recommend this course for anyone who wants to know "how the sausage is made" with regards to how policies are instigated, influenced and interpreted by many different political entities in Washington DC.

sections.goodFor: Anyone curious about social impact or social ventures, including experienced impact professionals wanting formal frameworks for efficacy, financial sustainability and scale.
sections.notFor: Students wanting quantitative rigor or a genuine critique of capitalism - one detailed comment says data is thin and root causes go unaddressed; non-business students may find it disorienting.
sections.workloadNote: Weekly cases and readings that vary week to week plus a group project; one says homework is not heavy for a 3-unit class but you must keep up. Sessions run 6-9pm.
sections.gradingBasis: Group project plus case preparation and class discussion; specific weights not described.
sections.redFlags: One long critique: readings/discussions assume a capitalist frame, normalize burnout, use little data, and instructors lacked answers on root causes; 1-2 others say it is effectively a speaker series.
sections.quote: be prepared and wary for the class to be extremely capitalistic without much data/room for counterarguments
comments: yes
Yes. The courses attempts to teach a meaningful topic and the instructors have gone above and beyond!

Yes, I would highly recommend the course to students who are curious of what social impact is and what different business models are evolving in the space. It is quite comprehensive in the degree of information that the course covers.

Absolutely yes. This is one of the most thoughtfully designed and meaningful courses I've taken at Haas. Gloria and Kristin bring complementary strengths — rigor, structure, and deep expertise paired with real-world entrepreneurial insight and inspiring leadership. The frameworks are immediately applicable, the cases are rich, and the discussions are some of the most engaging in the program. If you care about social impact, want to understand how real
organizations balance mission and sustainability, or simply want to learn from two outstanding educators, this class is a must-take.
Yes, I would. However, I would say this course isn't for everyone. I think this class represents the heart and soul of what any MBA student/graduate from Haas should both understand and value.
Yes! Amazing structure for a class. Studying the cases, solving challenges for them and then hearing from the people who lived that experience. Love it!

Good speakers. Strongly recommend considering your stamina for a night class (ours was 6-9 PM). Hopefully feedback has encouraged them to delve deeper into business models rather than strategy frameworks.

Yes, I would definitely recommend this course! The amazing line up of guest speakers makes it for such a fun, insightful and inspiring class. Tied to all the different concepts and theories we learn, this is a great mix of theory and practice. I've definitely learned a lot about the Social Sector and I'm looking forward to finding more ways to get involved with companies with companies that care about doing good in the world.
Interesting course, register if you want to essentially take a speaker series that centers around social impact from different organizations.

Yes, I would definitely recommend this class to all students, who wants to make some social impact, or just to learn about this world, or make culture better in their current workplace or just get inspired. Every class was amazingly inspirational with great speakers and subjects to learn. I think this class is one of the most important classes in Haas I would highly recommend this course to other students. This class provided frameworks to view business models and the world broadly, not just within social impact. I was able to apply my learnings to several of my other classes. It is well worth the time.

Yes because it allows for the tip of the iceberg to be encountered around social issues, but be prepared and wary for the class to be extremely capitalistic without much data/room for counterarguments. When issues and questioning of the status quo came up, many times, the instructors didn't have the answers or relied on conceptual concepts. Math or data isn't used much in this class to back up arguments rather than descriptive statistics. This class allows someone to be creative around solving social issues, but at its underlying core, the course doesn't answer the crucial answer in its entirety of how do you solve or combat social issues. The course feels that it helps one brainstorm bandaid business oriented solutions without exploring issues at its core and how to truly combat it. Moreover, the course makes a lot of excuses for the pitfalls of capitalism and expects it to be passed off. For example, when discussing compensation structures and how they're centered around the course's impact triangle concept, it became dicey with no solutions offered. One thing to point out is that readings really push the capitalist perspective to social issues rather than diverse issues, particularly in overworking workers and labor by stretching them thin for value. Burnout is accepted and normalized. Another example would be each business leader that came in already operated with mindsets that they're doing their best without much emphasis on how they're solving the underlying root causes of each problem. All in all, the course allows for a student to be challenged and explore different models out there and it's good to address the overlaying present issues, but not great at addressing underlying issues and deriving a model from there. Case studies, videos, and resources are great!

I think it makes sense for students at Haas to take this class. But it's a little disorienting for students outside of the business school...sometimes conversations about equity and how it plays into profitable business models is tough and feels like they are two separate things that can't always exist together

Yes, 100% recommend for all Haas students to take. From each case study, I felt like I learned more about strategy than in our core strategy class. What you'll learn is that nonprofit space is even more complicated for for profit because of the tension between public good and maintaining the business. You'll learn that even for-profit can have a net impact. And most of all, you'll get professors and be surrounded by students who actually care about making a change in society. You'll also be able to ask many questions to leaders in these spaces and get guidance and mentorship from Gloria and Kristin. These are gems who will guide you on your journey as a social entrepreneur. Yes! I've been in the social impact space (across nonprofit, foundaiton and corporate) for 10 years and havent been formally trained in some of these topics so being grounded in that was very applicable and relevant for me than other business classes. Some topics only touch the surface but the frameworks is helpful to take with you. Group projects take a bit of work and readings vary week to week in terms of load but otherwise, for a 3 unit class there's not heavy homework --just need to keep up to get the most out of class. Loved the thoughtfulness Kris and Gloria put into structuring and framing the class - with amazing energy. Also they make an effort to built class culture and connections so you'll get to mingle with everyone throughout the course. Top class for me!

YES. Any student who is remotely curious about social impact or applying their skills for good should take this class. Yes, you'll learn about practical frameworks to understand efficacy, financial sustainability, and scale that any entrepreneur or operator can apply in their work. However, the real differentiator this class offers is the wisdom and inspiration that comes week over week from exceptional guest speakers across all sectors of impact. You'll also connect with fellow impact-focused or curious students across Haas and Goldman, which is a fantastic way to meet other students. Highly recommend this rare experience.
Great "Feeling of being together" - class spirit is unmatched
Yes, I would. I think I found that the speakers who were most practical and less just giving life advice were the most useful to me.
YESSSSSSSSSS.
It's worth my 6-9pm, their effort, and how they design the class, set the engagement was unreal!
Absolutely. Extremely relevant case studies. Strong through-lines. The class has a great spine.
yes!
Take this class if you're interested in starting a social venture! Or even to learn more about different possible types of ventures.

sections.goodFor: Students interested in how AI both harms and helps sustainability - circularity, waste, water, energy - who want practitioner speakers and real examples.
sections.notFor: Students who want discussion and hands-on work over speaker panels; one wants more group discussion, another wants it expanded into a week-long immersion with a pitch competition.
sections.workloadNote: Thin evidence (10 comments). Very easy lift: only short assignments before each session; sessions run 10-3:30 rather than a full Sunday. First offering of the course.
sections.gradingBasis: Short pre-session assignments; not detailed further.
sections.redFlags: Two students note the speaker lineup skews heavily toward Google (one instructor comes from Google) and ask for diversified speakers/company content.
sections.quote: Really great speakers that mostly come from Google, and even if you are skeptical of Google, the speakers welcome questions.
comments: Yes, engaging class facilitation and discussions. Interesting guest speakers.

As the first iteration of this class I was very impressed with how quickly they put the curriculum together and how we talked about the intersection of AI and multiple aspects of sustainability including circularity, waste, water, energy and much more. There were really great speakers but I do think the class was a little biased towards Google and speakers from Google, given one of the professors comes from Google. This is not necessarily a bad thing, but I imagine they will try to diversify speakers and maybe company content to include other companies. I would recommend this class if you are interested in how AI is both affecting and helping with sustainability.
This class was very interesting. I can honestly say my perspective was broadened.
Yes
I will definitely. I love the class

I really enjoyed taking this class as we got to learn from organizations and leaders about real examples of the relationship of climate and AI. It was a very easy lift class - only short assignments before each session - and each class was very enjoyable to sit through.
Yes but I think the course needs more group discussion rather than speaker talks.

Great class that has the perfect time from 10 - 3:30 rather than the whole Sunday. Assignment load is light and helps to increase learning. Really great speakers that mostly come from Google, and even if you are skeptical of Google, the speakers welcome questions.
Yes, I wish this class was a week long immersion class with more speakers and potentially a formal venture pitch competition.
Yes

rows.title: Private Equity Leveraged Buyouts
rows.terms: 2021 Fall;2022 Spring;2022 Fall;2023 Spring;2023 Fall;2024 Spring

sections.goodFor: Students pivoting into or exploring PE, LBOs, M&A, investment banking, or search funds/ETA; repeatedly called one of the highest-ROI classes at Haas, accessible even without prior finance experience, with an organized, engaging practitioner instructor.
sections.notFor: Those with real prior PE/M&A experience (several found material introductory or repetitive) or students uninterested in finance; a few in the 2-unit fall section felt the reading load was excessive for the credit.
sections.workloadNote: The 1-unit weekend format is light for the value delivered, but the 2-unit fall co-taught version was repeatedly called heavy, with one or two 20-30 page cases weekly plus team assignments.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (5+ comments): the 1-unit format is too short to go deep on LBO modeling. A few fall-section comments (3) called the 2-unit version overloaded with reading and somewhat repetitive.
sections.quote: The highest ROI class I've taken at Haas. Highly recommended!

rows.title: Marketing Research: Tools and Techniques for Data Collection and Analysis
rows.disagree: High rating, but comment tone is mixed or negative

sections.goodFor: Students interested in user research, PM, or marketing analytics who want practical survey design plus SPSS/Python skills they can put on a resume.
sections.notFor: Students who need consistent, well-paced instruction - several call the class 'kind of a mess' with inconsistent sessions and a jarring jump into heavy statistics.
sections.workloadNote: Called low-lift overall, but assignments are time-consuming and the back half turns statistics-heavy after an easy start; semester-long research project with a real business.
sections.gradingBasis: Assignments (some shown as 'x/0 points' but actually graded), SPSS/Python analysis work, and a semester-long marketing research project.
sections.redFlags: 3-4 students: inconsistent sessions with no takeaway, 'the class overall was kind of a mess', easy first half that fails to prepare for a stats-heavy second half, '0 point' assignments graded.
sections.quote: You will find out on the last day of class that the "x/0 points" assignments are actually graded. Goodluck:)
comments: The class is lowlift and great content. I found the final project to be really interesting. However, the class sessions are inconsistent where some are super interesting and some lack a "takeaway." You will find out on the last day of class that the "x/0 points" assignments are actually graded. Goodluck:)
No personally.
Absolutely. I think both the course and instructor are some of the best that I have taken at Haas.
yes

This is an amazing class - would highly recommend especially if you're interested in user testing, and research! Imo, it's pretty applicable too if you're interested in PM and want to think about ways to gather data from your users. I learned a relatively good amount of things for a relatively low-lift class.

Overall, yes, I would recommend this course to other students. The assignments, while time consuming, were very worthwhile and gave an opportunity for practical applications of marketing research tools. I do wonder why this isn't an AI course, as we spent the duration of the semester working with an actual business on a marketing research question

I'm torn. I think the SPSS teachings and how to do data analysis was helpful and learning what types of questions, etc. to ask in surveys, etc. were helpful but the class overall was kind of a mess. If you can learn this content in another class with a professor with higher ratings, I'd go for that. The ratings from the previous year are confusing to me. TAKE THE COURSE! I would 100%. It's a class that caught me by surprise honestly. Would've never thought it was going to be one of my favorites. What made it great:
- Funny professor
- Small class, engaging discussions
- Very polished content - you can see Leif has tested many ways of teaching the material and this is a close to final version that works
- Assignments are genuinely enjoyable (Google Trends assignment specially)
- Highly valuable: I interned in a Marketing Analytics team and would've loved to have all this knowledge before. You can make an impact with this.
Another thing I've talked to other students about, is that there is some overlap with Data and Decisions. This is better. It's a more practical, more fun way of learning to analyze datasets.
Absolutely!

I would recommend this class 100%. If you take this class, be prepared to get what you want out of it -- you can add SPSS and Python as a new skill on your resume if you pay attention, or you can not show up/not do assignments and still learn general takeaways. But, don't take either outcome out on Prof. Nelson, he's really nice and trying! Yes, I think you get a good sense of the tools and attitudes necessary to examine and question data. Some classes can be slower than others but generally covers a lot of interesting topics
I would not recommend the course as it is now. The first few classes felt way too easy and didn't prepare us for the statistics heavy second half of the semester.

sections.goodFor: Anyone curious about VC or impact investing, beginner or experienced - you effectively do an associate's job for a semester and build a founder/Haas network; one landed an internship from it.
sections.notFor: Students who can't commit real time, or who want a lecture-structured class - it is mostly independent learning and your experience depends on a randomly assigned team.
sections.workloadNote: Short structured crash course in new venture finance up front, then roughly three months of real VC work - founder calls, sourcing, due diligence - largely independent and team-driven.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; work is team due diligence on real startups plus a brief front-end frameworks module. Grading itself is never discussed.
sections.redFlags: Two students flag that a good part of the experience depends on your randomly assigned group, and stress the real time commitment and heavy independent learning. No other complaints in 23 comments.
sections.quote: Unfortunately, good part of the class experience depends on your group and that is random, but if you have a neutral or good group and you're invested in the class, you'll learn a lot in practice.
comments: Absolutely! I keep telling everyone this is my MBA capstone, because it brings together everything I've learned in the MBA. I feel like I've actually gotten VC experience and have built up a pretty cool network of Haasies and founders Yes!
Absolutely. If you are even slightly curious about investing and impact investing, this class is great for intro as well as for experienced professionals.
Yes. Really knowledgeable professor.

Yes with the caveat it does depend on the team you get placed with, which is selected for you. This course is great because it gives real exposure and practice to startups, business models and funding. I got so much more out of this than a lecture and appreciate the hands on learning

Absolutely, take this class if you want to get a real experience of what it is like to be a venture capitalist. yes, 1000%. super practical crash course in new venture finance followed by a real application of VC investing for 3 months. one of the best semesters I've had at Haas.
YES - one of the best applied innovation classes I've taken! I took this and IBD and got great takeaways from both - the more real life application we can do in the classroom the better!
Yes, if you are a beginner in this space.

For anyone interested in VC, social impact, or impact investing, this is a must-take class! It's a lot of independent learning but I've learned more in this semester than I have in most other classes. If you're on the fence, take it! Absolutely. I took this class because I was curious about impact VC. I got that and so much more out of this class. I really owe my future career aspirations to this class.

Highly recommend. This was one of the most impactful courses to truly understanding the work of a VC investor. I learned a lot &, more importantly, had the chance to put my learnings into practice with numerous calls with startups Great class and one of the best I've taken at Haas.

YES, as long as you're committed to spending a solid time on it. Unfortunately, good part of the class experience depends on your group and that is random, but if you have a neutral or good group and you're invested in the class, you'll learn a lot in practice. Jeep and Adair are inspiring, knowledgeable and extremely accessible. One of my favorite classes!

I really learned a lot from this course - this course really teaches you how to be VC. I talked with many inspiring founders and learned a ton about the industry. There is a lot of work especially team work but the more time you spend the more rewarding it is.
Absolutely - best class I've taken.
Yes
If you are interested in how the VC due diligence process works from either the founder or the VC persepective, this course is awesome!

I would absolutely recommend this course! This was my favorite class at Haas. I learned a lot about impact investing. Take this if you're curious what impact investing is like. You do the job for a few months and can see if it's for you. This experience also helped me land an internship in the space.
Yes., Great course to take if you are interested in learning more about how venture capital works and being able to see it happen in action.
Yes,I've recommended the class to everyone who asked for what class to take in Spring

Absolutely. This class was very informative and took us through the journey of a what an associate working VC might do over the course of their company search. I liked that there was a brief structured portion of the class where we learned about frameworks and other basic industry knowledge, and that we had plenty of time for application in the real world.
This is the best course at Haas! You get to be an actual VC! Take this course even if you don't want to do VC, its just really good experience!!!

sections.goodFor: VC-curious students without venture experience; you act as an investor all semester with founder meetings and real diligence. One says it's the first Haas VC class that isn't 'bro'-dominated.
sections.notFor: Anyone who has already worked in venture, students not truly interested in VC (the workload will grate), and those primarily drawn by the impact framing.
sections.workloadNote: Same section as Kline's listing. Not quantified but called a heavy lift and time-intensive; about half the course is lab time, and the load scales with how far your team pushes sourcing and diligence.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; minimum assignment requirements plus sourcing, due diligence and pitch deliverables
sections.redFlags: 2 students say the 'Impact' name is a misnomer - the class de-emphasizes impact for market-rate returns. Experience is highly team-dependent; the $75k check size limits deal access.
sections.quote: You have to plan on having a lot of time to do out of class work. This is a time intensive projec- based course... Make sure your schedule allows you the time you need to do the work
comments: Yes
Absolutely. I wish I was able to take it sooner (it bid out when I was a first year). One of the most practical classes I took at Haas.
Yes. I believe anyone interested in venture capital and financing young companies with high potential should take this course.
yes! so fun getting our hands dirty with sourcing and due diligence. I realize there's still a lot of quant concepts I don't fully understand, but perhaps that is the reality of the industry.

Yes -- both Jeep and Adair were phenomenal instructors, and I found the overall course to be worthwhile, especially if you are aspiring to be in VC or otherwise just exploring it as a potential pathway. You really do get to act as a VC for the course of the semester, so it's a great opportunity to see how you like it and build some experience. The workload can be what you make of it -- if you/your team want to go all in, you could spend endless time sourcing and screening deals, diligencing, etc; you can fulfill minimum assignment requirements with a lot less work, though, if you don't feel passionate about investing a ton of time.

Will add that the "Impact" naming is a bit of a misnomer -- from day 1, the class de-emphasizes impact and focuses heavily on market-rate returns. Be warned if you are primarily taking this for the "Impact" spin, and know that it's really just traditional VC with a hint of impact framing.

This is a great class if you want to experience being a VC with lower stakes than in the real world. It is a heavy lift class and you need to be prepared to spend a lot of time sourcing deals, meeting founders and doing due diligence on the companies. Your experience will be very team dependent so how much work you do also depends on how engaged your team is. The professors are phenomenal and are always very willing to help students throughout.
Yes would recommend
100%!! Really great class. Honestly just wish I took it earlier as it would have helped me a lot!!
Yes I do. There is no better way to connect with start-ups, than saying that we can invest in them. Also, helps understand what a good start up is.
Yes, great way to get your hands dirty and practice sourcing and evaluation.
Yes I'd recommend this class, you are thrown into the deep end but you learn how to be a VC in a very hands on way, so it's worth it

Yes! if you are interested in learning about what it is like to be a VC but also want to focus on impact investing, this is the course to take! you will learn so much about another world of VC but also, it was really neat to learn about all the differnt companies in the different sectors where impact is needed.

Yes, I would recommend as long as they are interested in VC and/or impact investing. It gives real life hands-on experience on sourcing, performing due diligence and pitching. However if you are not very interested, it will be a lot of work and you won't enjoy.

Yes I would highly recommend this class to anyone who is interested in early-stage technology or VC investing. Anyone who is dissuaded by the "impact" framing of the class should speak to a past student who will surely emphasize the practical learning from the class and the very professionally applicable nature of the content. If you're interested in the real VC experience, it's the class that you must take. Although the workload may be higher than in other classes, the hands-on experience as a VC and learning is truly something that you want to get out of your MBA program.
Strongly recommend - very good opportunity to think and evaluate as a VC
Yes, this is the most practical and fun course I've taken at Haas. Very much recommend for quality of instruction, for anyone interested in impact investing or VC

If you have never done anything in venture before, then I 100% recommend this class. It's exactly what you would get from a venture internship, and Adair and Jeep provide a safe space to explore and learn. They are open, direct, and honest. I greatly appreciated their feedback. If you have been in venture before, then I don't think you need to take this class. I would invest your time learning something new in another Applied Innovation class.

Adair is a seasoned educator. You can tell that she is passionate about teaching and she really tries to decrease the amount of busy work in class. Jeep is a great investor. She's got incredible stories about what she has invested in and really encourages individuals to find their own passions / areas of investment. Both professors give up a lot of time to help students enter the vc space and riff off of each other. This is the first VC class I've taken at Haas where it's not a "bro" culture dominated space. Would highly recommend if you're interested in VC and/or talking to entrepreneurs. I would definitely recommend the Haas Impact Fund for those who are looking for hands on VC experience. It's a really fun class because you are actively sourcing real deals, so you meet with founders and do due diligence with real financials and materials from early stage companies. For EWMBA students - you have to get to campus by 4pm for a few weeks in the beginning of the semester, but then the rest of the semester you don't need to go to campus because you're coordinating remotely with your team. So it's actually quite flexible which can be especially good for EWMBA students. Lastly, Jeep and Adair are fantastic professors - getting to learn from them is a privilege. Really cool course but be prepared to dedicate the time and effort. The 75k check size is a bit of a challenge so be prepared to build and use your networks to access deals and improve your sourcing funnel. Adair and Jeep are amazing and it's worth taking the course just to work with them. But I can't emphasize this enough - the course requires time and there aren't any shortcuts at the end of the day so make sure you know what you're signing up for. Absolutely! Great way to learn what it takes to be a VC and guided by supportive, sharp advisors who bring experience from the field.

I would recommend this experiential learning course to anyone who is interesting in gaining quick learning and hands- on experience in VC. The impact part of the course is also meaningful, but it does not take away from the VC-learning aspect of the course. You have to plan on having a lot of time to do out of class work. This is a time intensive projec- based course; similar in the vein of time commitment to clean tech to market etc. Make sure your schedule allows you the time you need to do the work; as long as this is well set up for you, the course and instructors will deliver an awesome learning experience.
I would definitely recommend Haas Impact Fund to a fellow student. The class's hands-on-experience and material created a learning experience unique in the program. I really enjoyed this class.

I'd recommend this course to the students who are prepping to get into VC. It's a great class to network with VCs and founders. I've learned a lot from professors, mentors, founders, and investors. There is a lot of self-study involved as well, since half of the course is lab time.
Take this class if you want to work on investing for a potential move into the field (or to learn about being an angel).

rows.title: Designing Futures: Technology & Society
rows.terms: 2021 Spring;2021 Fall;2023 Spring;2024 Spring;2025 Spring;2026 Spring

sections.goodFor: Students wanting a creative, non-traditional break from analytical MBA classes - design thinking, futures scenarios, abstract discussion with strong facilitators.
sections.notFor: Students wanting technical, data-driven or immediately applicable business content; one calls it 'effectively creative writing', and teams are assigned rather than chosen.
sections.workloadNote: Low-lift 1-unit course: readings plus an assigned-team scenario project and discussion. One student notes the one-unit format feels somewhat fast.
sections.gradingBasis: Team scenario/futures project and class discussion; grading not discussed.
sections.redFlags: One of 22 found parts a waste of time and had a difficult team-project experience; teams are assigned, not chosen.
sections.quote: It's a fun, lightweight course- effectively creative writing. If you're looking for something off the beaten path and very soft-skill, this is it.
comments: Yes, it is a short course for you to explore future scenarios of an industry you might be interested on. It includes a framework for analyzing future scenarios that help structure thoughts and discussions.

Yes! I think it's a fun class and provides an alternate perspective on strategy formation from the traditional "gather the data, make a hypothesis, drive to it." It's also a great class to reflect on big problems that you may not think about in depth otherwise.

I would absolutely recommend this course. It is somewhat fast in this one-unit iteration, but the instructors are good people and thoughtful guiders of discussion. It could easily have devolved into something ungrounded and nebulous, and it's a credit to both the instructors and the rest of the class that it did not.

I highly recommend this class! It was very provocative, fun and different compared to other classes I've taken at Haas. Come with an open mind and willingness to challenge your beliefs and work in groups that you won't be able to choose. I am sure I will use the reflections from this class a lot in my professional life.
10/10 amazing class! The most engaging and estimulating I had during my MBA. 2 hours of my week where I forgot about the existence my cell phone.

yes!!

Extremely recommended. Super informative, different and fun class of the MBA.

sections.goodFor: Students interested in innovation, design, tech, social impact, policy or systems change who are open to ambiguity and want non-linear frameworks (signals, scenarios, storytelling).
sections.notFor: Students who want traditional structured MBA frameworks or dislike creative/unstructured work; also take it in a light unit semester so you have time to think.

sections.quote: The course is strongest if you are open to ambiguity and interested in thinking beyond traditional MBA frameworks.
comments: Yes. This is such a unique and fun class at Haas. A critique I have had of some of the other classes I have taken is that it can often feel like you're being given busy work. Everything in this class felt intentional and helped us get to where we needed to go, even if it didn't feel like that in the moment. Take this class and actually put some time and effort into the work.
Yes!! This is one of the best and most powerful courses I've taken at haas. In a moment of rapid change, it's one of the few classes that teaches a structure for how to think about the future.
I would! Great conversations. I looked forward to this class every week. With all this uncertainty, this class teaches to accept and think three steps ahead

Yes. I would recommend this course to students who want a more creative, expansive class that still connects back to strategy, technology, business, and society. The course is strongest if you are open to ambiguity and interested in thinking beyond traditional MBA frameworks. It pushes you to use signals, scenarios, and storytelling to explore how the future might unfold, which felt different from most Haas classes in a good way. I would especially recommend it for students interested in innovation, design, tech, social impact, policy, or systems change.

I ABSOLUTELY recommend. If you're looking for a class that helps you think where "disruption" comes from and non- linear frameworks to understand the world, this is your class. Also recommend to do it when you're not maxxed in units so you have time to think about the assignments and dive into the frameworks. Also expect to give "life" to your own rabbit holes and dystopian/utopian futures - which was really fun:)

Yes! They were all exposed to IDEO at a point in their careers and provides best in class design thinking methods I loved this class!! Was one of my favorites at Haas, really stretched my thinking, and was well executed class. I really appreciate that this class helps shift my way of thinking and prompts more outside the box ways of seeing the world and thinking about trends and futures. I think this is a very applicable class for strategic business thinking, but beyond that a really fun way explore the edge of the latest trends and shifts shaping our world today. Really excellent teaching team, great structure, tight syllabus, high ROI, fun creative class.

Yes! This course is way different thana most of the courses in Haas. This a course that takes you out of the comfort zone, it challenge your traditional structure of thinking and take your imigination to places you won't imagine The frameworks learned during the course were in stark contrast to the standard business education, and were incredibly generative for thinking about the future of tech, work, and life given changes we see in every facet of life due to AI and more. The workload was manageable and made sense for the duration and credit for the class. I only wish this could have been a bit longer of a course (~10 weeks) so that we could dig deeper into the scenarios and learn to internalize the frameworks more.

Yeah definitely! You need to be someone who's willing to embrace their more creative / unstructured thinking side to enjoy this class. That exercise in and of itself has me thinking more critically about the world around me, and I think the skills I built in this class will be valuable in my future career endeavors.

DEFINITELY. 100% my favorite course. It massaged my brain in a way that other Haas classes have not. I loved how much creativity and collaboration came out of it. Plus, the teaching team gives INCREDIBLE feedback.

Absolutely! Definitely take this class if you care about where the future of things are headed (you should). Honestly think this should be part of the core curriculum. It's such a cool class, the frameworks are ones I will use in many fields, and it flexes a mental and creative muscle that I already see showing up outside of the classroom. It's also a lot of fun and wonky and nice balance to some of the more technical and traditional hard-skill MBA classes. And yet it's still a hard-skill, just an overlooked one. Take it, take it!

Interested course that made you think about the preferred world you want to live in. Required group efforts for almost every assignment with quick turnarounds, but fun if you enjoy brainstorming and unique presentations as a way to think outside the box.
YES! This has been my favourite class at Haas, and has genuinely impacted the way I view the world. I'll be looking for signals and reading op-eds from the future for years to come.

Yes! Such a fun class that makes you exercise your creative muscles and step outside of the usual business school content to imagine what the future of our society could look like based on current "signals" we notice out in the world. This was one of the few classes I've taken where I genuinely looked forward to the final presentations and seeing the creative futures my classmates had constructed.

Yes!! Very unique course that gives you an opportunity to practice thinking about the future in a structured way. I loved coming to class every week and it was genuinely fun to work on our final project, as you get to focus on a topic that interests you

yes!!

Yes, It's a different class from all of the business classes that I have taken at Haas and definitely a nice change to get you thinking outside the box.
Extremely recommended. Super informative, different and fun class of the MBA.

sections.goodFor: Students interested in innovation, design, tech, social impact, policy or systems change who are open to ambiguity and want signals/scenarios/storytelling tools beyond standard MBA frameworks.
sections.notFor: Students who want traditional structure, hard quantitative skills or clean answers. Several say take it when you are not maxed on units, since the assignments need thinking time.
sections.workloadNote: Group effort on almost every assignment with quick turnarounds, building to a self-chosen final project and presentation. Workload called manageable for the credits and explicitly not busy work.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear - assignments, group work and final presentations are described, but grading is never discussed.
sections.redFlags: None recurring. Two students wish the course ran longer (~10 weeks) so they could go deeper into scenarios and internalize the frameworks.
sections.quote: Required group efforts for almost every assignment with quick turnarounds, but fun if you enjoy brainstorming and unique presentations as a way to think outside the box.
comments: Yes. This is such a unique and fun class at Haas. A critique I have had of some of the other classes I have taken is that it can often feel like you're being given busy work. Everything in this class felt intentional and helped us get to where we needed to go, even if it didn't feel like that in the moment. Take this class and actually put some time and effort into the work.
Yes!! This is one of the best and most powerful courses I've taken at haas. In a moment of rapid change, it's one of the few classes that teaches a structure for how to think about the future.
I would! Great conversations. I looked forward to this class every week. With all this uncertainty, this class teaches to accept and think three steps ahead

Yes. I would recommend this course to students who want a more creative, expansive class that still connects back to strategy, technology, business, and society. The course is strongest if you are open to ambiguity and interested in thinking beyond traditional MBA frameworks. It pushes you to use signals, scenarios, and storytelling to explore how the future might unfold, which felt different from most Haas classes in a good way. I would especially recommend it for students interested in innovation, design, tech, social impact, policy, or systems change.

I ABSOLUTELY recommend. If you're looking for a class that helps you think where "disruption" comes from and non- linear frameworks to understand the world, this is your class. Also recommend to do it when you're not maxxed in units so you have time to think about the assignments and dive into the frameworks. Also expect to give "life" to your own rabbit holes and dystopian/utopian futures - which was really fun:)

Yes! They were all exposed to IDEO at a point in their careers and provides best in class design thinking methods I loved this class!! Was one of my favorites at Haas, really stretched my thinking, and was well executed class. I really appreciate that this class helps shift my way of thinking and prompts more outside the box ways of seeing the world and thinking about trends and futures. I think this is a very applicable class for strategic business thinking, but beyond that a really fun way explore the edge of the latest trends and shifts shaping our world today. Really excellent teaching team, great structure, tight syllabus, high ROI, fun creative class.

Yes! This course is way different thana most of the courses in Haas. This a course that takes you out of the comfort zone, it challenge your traditional structure of thinking and take your imigination to places you won't imagine The frameworks learned during the course were in stark contrast to the standard business education, and were incredibly generative for thinking about the future of tech, work, and life given changes we see in every facet of life due to AI and more. The workload was manageable and made sense for the duration and credit for the class. I only wish this could have been a bit longer of a course (~10 weeks) so that we could dig deeper into the scenarios and learn to internalize the frameworks more.

Yeah definitely! You need to be someone who's willing to embrace their more creative / unstructured thinking side to enjoy this class. For me, it was an awesome opportunity to get outside of my comfort zone and explore information and sources that I'm not usually accustomed to, and try to spend more time just thinking about signals and how they develop / where they're headed. That exercise in and of itself has me thinking more critically about the world around me, and I think the skills I built in this class will be valuable in my future career endeavors.

DEFINITELY. 100% my favorite course. It massaged my brain in a way that other Haas classes have not. I loved how much creativity and collaboration came out of it. Plus, the teaching team gives INCREDIBLE feedback.

Absolutely! Definitely take this class if you care about where the future of things are headed (you should). Honestly think this should be part of the core curriculum. It's such a cool class, the frameworks are ones I will use in many fields, and it flexes a mental and creative muscle that I already see showing up outside of the classroom. It's also a lot of fun and wonky and nice balance to some of the more technical and traditional hard-skill MBA classes. And yet it's still a hard-skill, just an overlooked one. Take it, take it!

Interested course that made you think about the preferred world you want to live in. Required group efforts for almost every assignment with quick turnarounds, but fun if you enjoy brainstorming and unique presentations as a way to think outside the box.
YES! This has been my favourite class at Haas, and has genuinely impacted the way I view the world. I'll be looking for signals and reading op-eds from the future for years to come.

Yes! Such a fun class that makes you exercise your creative muscles and step outside of the usual business school content to imagine what the future of our society could look like based on current "signals" we notice out in the world. This was one of the few classes I've taken where I genuinely looked forward to the final presentations and seeing the creative futures my classmates had constructed.

Yes!! Very unique course that gives you an opportunity to practice thinking about the future in a structured way. I loved coming to class every week and it was genuinely fun to work on our final project, as you get to focus on a topic that interests you

sections.goodFor: Students who like physical and mental challenge, have some hiking or backpacking interest, and want to test leadership styles in a low-risk, high-stress setting while bonding with classmates.
sections.notFor: Students wanting rigorous leadership theory - one calls the leadership component 'more fluff than substance'. Another wanted greater physical rigor and found the guides too hands-on.
sections.workloadNote: Thin evidence (9 comments). Workload is the expedition itself (Patagonia or Andes trek with NOLS/Vertical) plus classroom sessions with guest speakers beforehand; no weekly hours discussed.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear
sections.redFlags: 2 students: guest speakers weren't additive and classroom time would be better spent on team problem-solving and outdoor skills prep; 1 says the leadership framing is fluffier than the experience deserves.
sections.quote: It's a truly challenging experience that'll push you to your limits but in the midst of a well designed team and support setup... The leadership bit though - more fluff than substance I felt.
comments: Yes! It's a truly challenging experience that'll push you to your limits but in the midst of a well designed team and support setup. You'll definitely build confidence to pursue and achieve the extreme, and learn about the limits of your mind and body. The leadership bit though - more fluff than substance I felt.

Maybe. I felt that the guest speakers weren't necessarily additive to my learning experience or in preparing for the expedition part of the course. I think it would've been better to incorporate more in-person team problem solving exercises instead of sitting listening to the speakers. It would've also been helpful to dedicate a class on working on some outdoors skills so that all participants show up to their expedition better prepared and there's less time spent during the expedition on learning these skills. I would recommend that the instructors, NOLS or Vertical, be more hands off. And I would recommend that the physical rigor of the expedition be greater (I was on the Patagonia trip). Yes! This was one of the best classes I've taken so far because it went beyond teaching leadership as theory and gave hands on experience for how one leads and can improve.

Absolutely!! Such a unique experience that you truly can't get anyway else. An amazing way to truly get to know your strengths and weaknesses and try different styles of leadership in a lower risk environment

If you're someone that loves challenging yourself both mentally and physically and/or have basic backpacking or hiking experience, I highly recommend signing up for the Andes Trek. It's truly a once in a lifetime opportunity to experience high altitude mountaineering in a safe and well-resourced environment. The leadership aspect of this course also can't be oversold - it might be one of the most formative experiences I've had at Haas. If you're questioning whether to take the leap and sign up, do it!!
Yes - awesome course. Intro to backpacking and good opportunity to develop personal skills outside the classroom. Incredible opportunity to strengthen your leadership skills.

I would 100% recommend this opportunity and course! Getting out on the edge of our comfort is the best way to grow stronger and wiser both in business and the wilds. This is also an incredible trip to get to know classmates in extraction from the MBA environment.
I could not recommend Omri highly enough. Take every class he offers.
The most unique experience you'll have during your MBA: challenging, rewarding, surprising.
Be prepared and enjoy the ride!

sections.notFor: No commenter identifies who should avoid it; the only caveat raised is dense academic/research reading and a Thursday night slot.

comments: I would recommend this course if you are interested in the subject because the professors are very open to helping you with applying these concepts to real life topics / issues, and they provide good activities and projects that help you apply the concepts to real life topics / issues.

Yes I will. This class has small class size but this is one of my favorate classes at Haas. Both professors are great, supportive, knowledgable and authentic. We learn many concepts with real life examples.
Great class and really good tandem professors. Workload is pretty light, and while there's some heavy

Yes I think this is one of my favorite classes so far!

Love the course. Ellen and Rachel made a night class super fun and easy to participate. Definitely take a class with one or both of these professors.

LOVED this class, maybe my favorite so far at Haas! Would highly recommend to anyone who has any interest in psych and its applications to business. Genuinely sad it's over, which is crazy to say about a 3 credit evening class. Its a really fun and hands-on class. recommend people interested in UX and marketing space

Absolutely yes! This has been my favorite class this semester. I would recommend it to all my classmates, even those who aren't familiar with marketing. Ellen and Rachel made the class so engaging — even though it was on a Thursday night, I never missed a single session.

Yes!!! especially if you are interested in product! Rachel and Ellen are amazing and tailor the class to your needs so you can get the most out of the class! This class is what convinced me to finally launch my product and take it to the next step!!!!

If they are very interested in pharma, not introductory

yes

rows.title: Difficult Conversations: Conflict Lab
rows.disagree: High rating, but students split on whether it works

sections.goodFor: Anyone wanting practiced tools for conflict and difficult conversations; pairs well with Negotiations and Power & Politics. Many say it should be core.
sections.notFor: Students unwilling to be uncomfortable or to show up and participate; two doubt the tools survive consulting or intense corporate environments.
sections.workloadNote: Work is participatory rather than assignment-based: repeated role plays (including virtual sessions with volunteers) and substantial self-reflection. 'You get as much as you give'.
sections.gradingBasis: Attendance and active participation in role plays plus reflective work; not detailed further.
sections.redFlags: Two of 28 question the depth/realism of the role plays and whether the tools would actually work in consulting or other intense corporate environments.

comments: Absolutely! Such a fun and energetic class. You will be pushed out of your comfort zone in a supportive way and your personal and professional relationships will improve for the better
Yes, very important skills for conflict in both professional and personal relationships

Definitely - it shed light on the things I don't do well in conflict and is giving me a path to improve them! Yes. I would recommend. The course enabled me to re-evaluate my understanding and connection with conflict. I believe I will be a better leader in the future as a result.
Would highly recommend! Very engaging class and hands on learning
Yes! Highly reccomend if you want to learn and practice tools for difficult conversations. It requires commitment to the role plays and a lot of self reflection, so you have to be open to the process
I would definitely recommend this course for my fellow students.

I also feel that it would be great to have people from other schools have the opportunity to have this course. I think the main reason is that conflict is uncomfortable, and this class will make you less uncomfortable with it, and possibly even more curious about it and less afraid of putting your needs and perceptions on the table in order to reach a better situation after.
Yes! This class puts in you uncomfortable situations, and learned a ton. The frameworks and tools in this class are great for effectively navigating conflict in the real world.

ABSOLUTELY! I wish this class was in the core, as I feel that the world needs people to be better equipped to handle conflict in general. I think is a misunderstanding that people make that they don't need to improve this skill. At least in my experience, the best leaders are the ones who are skillful in dealing with conflict, and unfortunately as a society we're not taught this.

The class was really insightful into 3 things: (1) Finally understand my own conflict style and to recognize others (I never knew that conflict styles were actually a thing) (2) Open my mind and heart that conflicts can be solved without hurting my own boundaries (3) Learn a toolbox of how to have effective conversations and apologies
Additionally: Awesome to learn how to differentiate interpretations from observations, and how feelings and needs are so connected. This is REALLY insightful!!!!

Despite wishing that this course was in the core, I understand why this is the case. This is a class that you need to take with an open heart, and you'll get as much as you give. If you want to take this class, plan to attend and participate, as the experience gets much better with more people engaged. Also, the more you're open and ready to do
reflective/introspective work, the more you'll take out of this experience.

The instructors (Bree and Francesca) are also AMAZING! They bring so much energy to the class, are so thoughtful into creating an inclusive and learning environment that I wish it lasted longer. I absolutely leave this experience with a sensation that now I have a toolkit to help me during difficult conversations and conflicts.
YES

I definitely would recommend this class! It is one of the best classes at Haas. I learned so many new tools to navigate conflict, and I think Bree and Francesca created an incredible environment that felt psychologically safe, inclusive, and regenerative. This class is truly a gift.
Yes! Would recommend. Super exciting and creative and different than many classes

Maybe, I think I was more thoughtful about conflict during this time but I felt like the tools had varying degrees of usefulness. I just couldn't imagine them working in the world of consulting or other intense corporate environments. Would recommend
Great class

Absolutely! Everyone should be required to take this class. Being equipped to navigate conflict and difficult conversations is such a necessary skill — especially in the current climate in the world. They make the topic fun, approachable and just a joy. One of my favorite classes at Haas hands down.

Conflict Lab should be a core class. You will grow as a person. Highly recommended if you have the capacity! Yes, I believe this course gives students time to practice conflict and try different role plays
I would 100% recommend this course and professors. I especially liked the virtual sessions where we did role play with volunteers, that made the conflict more real.

Yes! I loved the class. It is very useful for work settings and for life. It may be uncomfortable to do the role playing but i learned so much about conflict and about myself. And it is also extremely fun. Bree and Francesca are the best! This course was great, I had never thought about a framework for conflict before and I feel like I left the course with tangible skills to tackle conflict in the real world. The framework is very helpful and the role plays help you practice different tools and strategies.
Absolutely 100%

I really enjoyed this course and found it valuable to reframe how I look at and deal with conflict. Keep an open mind, lean into things and the more you put in the more you get out of this experience.

I would recommend this course to other students. The numerous roleplays that touch on realistic situations that you encounter in the work place is very helpful for getting into the habit and practice of engaging in conflict. The frameworks and tools covered in class are helpful for the day to day as well. The space provided for reflecting on your own objectives, emotions, and needs is incredibly important for dealing with any kind of tension/conflict you may encounter. This class pairs will with other EQ classes like Negotiations and Power & Politics, because it allows you to put into practice some of the frameworks and mindsets overviewed in those classes to be a more effective
communicator and active listener.
Recommend very highly!
Yes. EVERYONE should take this class. It teaches you essential skills for the corporate world and your personal life. Of course. Lots of personal applications

Yes. She works so hard and genuinely cares about her students.
Best class of Haas
Highly recommend this course! Francesca works so hard to ensure that it's relevant for all of us, and it's a super engaging 10 weeks. I'll definitely be using some of the tools I learned in class!
Yes, this is a very personal and emotional class that creates value if you come open and clear in what you want to work on

Would recommend with caution. Good class to learn skills but sometimes the manufactured enthusiasm was a bit tiring Yes, practicing conflict is important as its an unavoidable part of life. Great course and practice.

Of course! This class is applicable to real-world contexts, and the instructor actively draws on our experiences to build out scenarios for the entire class to practice. I also love the continuity and sense of community among alumni that is built through the role-play volunteers and workshops:)
Yes, good way to understand conflict as something not to fear especially for conflict avoidant types
Yes - this class gave me great tools to be more effective in conflict and mediation
Yes! She's an expert in conflict since she's a professional corporate mediator

I'd definitely recommend. It's given me some helpful tools to use moving forward in professional and personal conflict. As a result of this class, I am much less conflict-avoidant since it feels less scary and hard!!
Yes!
Yes. I think this is an unmissable Haas class. It almost feels like a right of passage. I honestly wish it was a core class because I think that the people who need it most self select out of it.

No, I would not recommend this course in its current form, unless the syllabus evolves substantially. While the instructor is clearly caring, energetic, and committed to creating an interactive environment, the course itself did not deliver practical value.

I enrolled hoping to gain concrete tools for managing conflict, but much of the class focused instead on reflection, broad frameworks, and lightly developed exercises. For students seeking a highly practical, impactful course on conflict management, I do not think this class currently meets that standard. I would reconsider that view only if the syllabus were significantly redesigned to include stronger tools, more realistic exercises, and a much more applied approach.

NOT AT ALL. Only take Conflict Lab if Bree is co-teaching it or there is a fully new instructor team. Sadly, most overhyped class and instructor in my two years at Haas -- wish I could unbid and unenroll in this class to get my time back.
This class is an absolutely must for students at Haas. The community, the role playing, the care and thoughts put into designing it by the instructors...

Yes. This is an interesting course that is taken with the right amount of self reflection will help you a lot Great way to think about how to be more in your body and present during conflict. Reduces the perceived cost of conflict/interpersonal challenges.

sections.goodFor: Juniors/seniors and grad students about to earn income; first-gen and low-income students; internationals staying in the US; anyone with zero finance background.
sections.notFor: Freshmen or anyone with no income yet — retirement/tax/insurance content feels abstract. Internationals not staying in the US get less value. Already financially literate students learn less.
sections.workloadNote: Consistently light: 'workload is manageable and not heavy at all.' 2 hours of class/week plus supplemental videos, a 3-stage budgeting assignment, and consistent small weekly assignments.
sections.gradingBasis: Quizzes/exams testing details from the supplemental videos, assignments incl. the budgeting project, and attendance. Many take it P/NP.
sections.redFlags: Two specific gripes: an attendance policy that soured one student enough to withdraw their recommendation, and quizzes/exams testing specifics from the supplemental videos (2 mentions).
sections.quote: This class is much more worthwhile and useful for those who have been earning an income. This class focuses a lot on retirement funds/ tax/ insurance.
