sections.goodFor: Students interested in social change, social impact or nonprofit consulting who want an inspiring instructor, a strong practitioner network, and frameworks not taught elsewhere at Haas.
sections.notFor: Anyone wanting a light 2-unit class, or who is not interested in consulting deliverables - one student says the syllabus should be upfront that assignments are consulting-skills heavy.
sections.workloadNote: More work than students expect for a 2-unit class; assignments are time-intensive consulting simulations (pick an org, diagnose an issue, build a deck, present as if to a client). First-time offering.
sections.gradingBasis: Consulting-style assignments: pick an organization, identify an issue, build a deck, present as if to a client; plus discussion.
sections.redFlags: First offering: 2-3 say structure was unclear week to week ('building the ship as it was floating') and workload exceeds a 2-unit class; assignments are consulting decks, irrelevant to one non-consulting student.
sections.quote: it seemed like Steve was building the ship as it was floating and so it was unclear to me and other students what to expect on a week to week basis
comments: Yes; the course was one of the best/if not the best course that I have taken at Haas. This was precisely because Steve was the instructor, not based on the course curriculum. The way he engaged the students and iterated his course design was truly remarkable. I could clearly see the dedication that he has provided in every lecture. The positive energy that he brought was truly contagious. Berkeley was lucky to have Steve teach the course for MBA students. Easily one of the best classes I've taken during my time here. The learning in this class is so broadly applicable (life, work, school, etc.) and the way that the course is taught, it will stick with you more than for other classes. Steve is an extremely charismatic, passionate, and caring individual - this came through in how he led the course and interacted with students. The time you invest in this class has an exceptional return. Even if you don't have an interest in going into social impact, you will have many takeaways from this class.
Yes

1000% - one of the most interesting courses I took at Haas. It is more work thank you think it will be but it's worthwhile and really close to what you'd do in the professional world. I almost think part of this class should either replace or be combined with the core biz comm class for FTMBA.
Yes, but if the class structure improves.

Steve is well-versed in social change work and community building. He provided tangible examples of the concepts covered in class and has built a community of practitioners who served as guest speakers and added a great deal of context to the material. Steve is empathetic and brings hopes to these topics of social change that can feel heavy and difficult to change. The case studies and frameworks he introduced were helpful in breaking down complex problems and provided deep insights into how to change hearts and minds. As far as the course as a whole, it seemed like Steve was building the ship as it was floating and so it was unclear to me and other students what to expect on a week to week basis or how the full picture fit together. I think this primarily due to the fact that it was his time teaching, but with time and having had this first experience I have hope that the course will improve. That said, I would recommend the course to other students. It was a great way to overview the history of social movements (though mostly from a US context) and think through our personal theories of change. Expect to do a bit more work than you might think (though expectations may be more clear with future iterations of the class and more teaching experience from Steve), but you will learn a lot and be among students with similar values.

YES. Steve is superb: extremely experienced, personable, and organized. This is one of my favorite classes at Haas, and I can't believe I got to take it. Steve treats students like professional peers, which means that learning happens at a higher level than many classes. Be prepared that it is a lot of work (though hopefully Steve will take feedback to improve that in later semesters), but the work is relevant and valuable. Take this class, get to know Steve and his phenomenal and inspiring network, and have a great time with the other awesome people this class attracts. Yes, absolutley! This should be a core class
YES 100% if you want to think about things in a new way and be truly inspired, that is.

Overall, I expected this course to be more focused on social change and less consulting skills heavy. If I were planning to be a consultant, particularly in the social impact space, I would have found this course immensely valuable. As it is, the assignments were a lot of work, and seemed to simulate consulting projects -- pick an organization, identify an issue, build a deck, and present in class as if to the client. Because I'm not planning to be a consultant of any kind, I didn't find these assignments to be as relevant to me. Therefore, I wish the assignments had been a bit more diversified, or that the syllabus had been more up front that the course is geared towards consultant skills. Absolutely take this class. Learning from Steve was the highlight of my semester, and I am so thankful I will have him in my network for life. This course will push you to think differently, and the assignment themselves are great learning opportunities. If you are a little curious in social change, take this course.

One of the BEST classes I have taken at Haas. Steve truly cares about all the students, the content is phenomenal, and there is a lot of interesting concepts that aren't taught in other classes. At times, it can be a lot of work, but he does it in the best interest of the students. He is open to feedback and really makes sure students are learning and growing. I think you should absolutely take this class if you are interested in social impact - Steve is giving with his network and provides helpful critiques that felt similar to what I have received in the real world. If you are interested in nonprofit consulting in particular I think this class could be helpful.

Steve is very knowledgeable about social change and is committed to his students. I learned a lot about inspiring, leading, and strategy from the lens of large scale social change. Steve is funny, self-aware, asks for feedback, and actually takes it into account in order to improve the course. He cares a lot about outcome and brings a wide range of guest speakers. This is my favorite class that I've taken and you will learn a lot despite it only being a 2 unit course. I would! As someone who has worked in social impact for a decade, I was surprised that most of the content we learned about was new to me! Steve is incredibly passionate, joyous, knowledgeable, and caring. He really wants everyone to succeed and become better people. Great professor and interesting class!

Steve is super inspiring and an optimist. He takes this work seriously and wants you to too. It's not a skate-by class, but it's more interesting and fulfilling if you put effort into the discussions and assignments. Expect to produce consulting-style recommendations for scaling a movement. These were time-intensive but really valuable assignments. 100% recommend taking this class. Steve Naga-Mai is hands down the best professor I have ever had. Very passionate about Social Change, and someone who brought 110% of himself to the classroom. You will learn a ton about how large scale social change happens. You will also learn of a very compelling model to live by--he is a great leader, communicator, and person. If you take the class and life of social change (to some capacity) seriously, this class can really have an impact on you.

yes this course is awesome.

sections.goodFor: Students who care about climate policy and systems change and want a broad primer plus access to an exceptional slate of guest speakers and the Berkeley climate community.
sections.notFor: Anyone drawn by the 'Finance & Infrastructure' in the title — not emphasized. Students who've taken several climate classes find it repetitive; law school climate classes give more per credit.
sections.workloadNote: 'Very reasonable workload,' though one notes you must spend extra energy speaking up in class. Format is guest speakers plus discussion; assignments were criticized as unclear.
sections.gradingBasis: Class discussion/participation and assignments; several note assignments lacked clarity. Weights not discussed.
sections.redFlags: Title oversells finance/infrastructure (2); lacks focus and sequence, 'bites off too much' (3); assignments unclear (2); Libby less prepared than Kate (1); 1 says real insight comes from classmates, not profs.
sections.quote: Fantastic guest speakers. Very reasonable workload. Just super broad topic lacking a clear focus, sequence, and takeaway... Climate, infra, politics, and finance is sort of everything
comments: Absolutely worthwhile class to link together material that isnt otherwise inherently connected and through this class and the guest speakers we found a way to make remarkably intuitive connections to understand the ultimate goal of how to behave in a climate adapting world.

If you really care about climate policy, yes. Not so much if you're attracted to the "Finance and Infrastructure" parts of the title, which are not emphasized. Interesting class to get a feel for what a Public Policy degree feels like. Very theoretical, and fun class discussions. The real insights come from all the climate-interested people enrolled in the class rather than the profs themselves.

Maybe - if you have deep knowledge of the space and want to go deeper, but you have to be able to really make the experience into what you need it to be because it's a little all over the place as currently designed.

Yes, I would recommend this course to individuals interested in understanding the relevance of climate change and systems change. We dive into hairy problems and have an open dialogue where many viewpoints are welcomed. Great speakers who are experts in their fields.
YES - this class provides a holistic understanding of the challenges and solutions around climate change.

The course is more suitable for students who have much experience in climate and are planning to pursue a career in this path. Sutdents who just want to learn sth in Climate may find the course a bit dry...

I would absolutely recommend this class, especially as a person who had very little knowledge about approaching climate change from a policy and organizational lens. This class takes a broad approach which is great for people who are seeking to broaden their aperture in the climate space.

I would recommend this course to another student. It is a really engaging class grounded in real-world examples. Both professors are very engaged and willing to meet with students to gain a deeper understanding of course content. This course provides a high level overview of many different climate topics and Isa good primer for the space. What you get out of the course is what you put in to it, and it could be just that you got to hear from a lot of really cool people about really cool stuff, or that you took personal initiative to deep dive into one area of the course and came away with a really good understanding of that topic.

This is a good class for getting a foundation in climate infrastructure and considerations. The topics covered in class were helpful for understanding the landscape of government interventions and financing instruments. Kate was a more engaging and prepared lecturer than Libby, but Libby often had an interesting perspective given her role as former Mayor Oakland. The two were a good balance, but a few improvements to the class like clearer assignments would have improved the overall course experience.
most phenomenal course I took at Haas. Be prepared to work a little, and spend extra energy speaking up in class as this is more challenging than typical MBA courses.

Totally recommend - for people who want to learn about climate, it's a great place to hear about the most topical discussions going on at the global, federal and state level. For students with more experience in climate, it's a relatively laid-back class where you can come, have good conversations, hear from and meet amazing speakers and connect with the broader Berkeley climate community.

Yes, I would. Great professors with cool experiences. Fantastic guest speakers. Very reasonable workload. Just super broad topic lacking a clear focus, sequence, and takeaway... Climate, infra, politics, and finance is sort of everything... bites off too much.

I would definitely recommend this course! Kate and Libby bring in an extraordinary slate of speakers and have great experience to share with students. If you're interested in the subject matter, I think it's a must-take.

Yes. It's a good politics and sustainability course. However, I think I'd take a law school climate class over this if I had already taken several climate classes (my case), as some of the information from this class was repetitive from other classes. If you haven't taken many climate classes, you definitely would take this if you're interested in the political side. Note that it focused a lot on CA and the US, but good to have the basis/ model and know how to expand that out to other regions or countries. The law school climate classes just give you a better marginal benefit per credit hour than this class with less duplicative information if you've already taken many business school climate classes. Yes - interesting to see policy and business views come together.

Yes — this course is one of the few that truly connects climate policy, financing, and infrastructure in a way that feels both practical and immediately relevant to real-world challenges. Kate Gordon and Libby Schaaf create an engaging environment that blends policy insight with lived experience, making the class valuable for anyone interested in the intersection of climate and decision-making.

I would recommend this if you are interesting from learning from and meeting with incredibly accomplished people, but keep in mind that this really is /a lot/ of work outside of class and you need to love your team and have some interest in your ideas.

sections.goodFor: Future managers who will deal with labor, and anyone interested in organizing, social change, or critiques of corporate power - even skeptics.
sections.notFor: Students who already have union or labor-organizing experience - one found the content obvious and the class a 'long and winding walk through unions'.
sections.workloadNote: Repeatedly called low-lift with little outside coursework; class is discussion-driven with a capstone organizing project run with the whole class as one group.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear; class discussion and a whole-class capstone organizing project.
sections.redFlags: One student says it is only an intro to unions and does not teach management-union interaction; experience depends heavily on who else is in the discussion-based class.
sections.quote: Your experience will largely depend on the makeup of your class, as it's highly discussion based and also involves a group project where the entire class is one group.
comments: Yes! its a fun course and pretty low lift!
Yes absolutely. This is one of the best classes I've taken at Haas. Roy is a gem!

This class was not at all what I thought it would be. It was kind of a long and winding walk through unions rather than teaching me how management and unions can better interact. Maybe some of it felt obvious to me because I have prior experience with unions, but I don't think any of the content was especially interesting. I'm not sure this class would be useful unless you're looking for an intro to unions.

Definitely would recommend. This class is so different from the other Haas courses but so necessary. Very few of us know the dynamics of labor organizing, yet it is one of the most powerful countervailing forces we have against corporate power and capitalism's shortcomings. Take this class, even if you're skeptical!
Yes, simply because of his passion and experience, and how underrepresented this subject matter is for most MBAs. OF COURSE

Interesting class taught by a talented professional faculty member. Your experience will largely depend on the makeup of your class, as it's highly discussion based and also involves a group project where the entire class is one group. Overall I'm glad I took the course.
Yes, defintely! I believe that if Roy agrees to teach a course, he is as knowledgeable and enthusiastic as he was for this one, so you should try to take it!
Yes - this class covers something unique that a lot of other classes don't and the capstone was really interesting working with all the class to organize.

Definitely! This was one of the most high-impact classes I took at Haas. It's extremely valuable for anyone interested in alternatives to capitalism, social change, and/or organizational power dynamics. Roy does a great job facilitating discussions and the workload is very manageable.
Yes!

This course is a must-do class. Understanding organizing (and what it entails) is a key component to LIFE, not just business and Roy does a wonderful job of breaking it down and creating an open, authentic space for people to learn and share their experiences.
Instructor is great and charismatic, doesn't require a lot of outside course work which is great if you are looking for that!

Definitely would recommend! Roy is a fantastic engaging professor. It's a relatively low lift class that has high value and offers a very different perspective from the other courses students will encounter at Haas.
Absolutely!!
I genuinely think that every person should take this class as many people in this program will go into management roles. So important to know how to collaborate with labor!!

sections.goodFor: Students who have not worked in highly political organizations and want frameworks for navigating power, influence, and organizational dynamics; many call it second-year core material, and Sameer is widely praised as one of the best discussion facilitators at Haas.
sections.notFor: Students who have already navigated multiple political workplaces or taken Negotiations, Leading People, or LeadComm, since several flagged heavy content overlap; also not for those wanting hands-on practice over case discussion, and a vocal minority preferred the other section of this course.
sections.workloadNote: Heavy weekly reading, typically two long cases per class, described as a big jump from the core; you get out what you put in.
sections.gradingBasis: A few commenters said grading leans heavily on two papers and felt like a black box with little guidance on how to improve.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (6+ comments): overlap with Negotiations and other leadership courses; several call the class overhyped relative to its reputation; a few recommend the other instructor's section instead; two note opaque grading on the papers.
sections.quote: Nothing in this class is earth-shattering, but Sameer is one of the best, if not the best, classroom facilitators I've had at Haas.

sections.goodFor: Anyone who has never led a team, or who thinks they are already a strong leader - the class targets your assumptions and biases.
sections.notFor: Students who want a concrete, immediately usable leadership toolkit; two say it is long on reflection and short on applied tools.
sections.workloadNote: 'Lots of reading required'; class time uses activities, simulations and surveys. No other workload detail given.
sections.gradingBasis: Participation is heavily incentivized; class activities/simulations and reflection. Qualtrics surveys used (one complaint).
sections.redFlags: Two students wanted more applied advice/toolkit rather than concept; one asks him not to use Qualtrics; one notes early-course criticism that the instructor then addressed.
sections.quote: This class was really interesting and should be taken by anyone who has never been a leader or who thinks they're a really good leader already
comments: Yes I would recommend this class because it was a way to rethink how I approached leading people and leadership topics.
Yes - Don's class is incredibly broad and comprehensive but really does a good job of getting you to question your assumptions

Don brought a genuine enthusiasm for course material, application of concepts to class activities and simulations, and allowed for rich and productive class discussions. I recommend his course for the core Leading People requirement. Yes. We learned a lot about effective leadership
Yes! Class covers great points
Yes
Would fully recommend; Don Moore is a fantastic instructor with very deep subject knowledge.
Yes, absolutely.

Absolutely.

Yes

Don got a lot of criticism at the beginning of the course, but he listened, changed, and we are all better for it. Yes
Yes
Yes! Don made a big impact to my MBA experience and I've learned so much from this class.
Yes, I would he is experienced and could learn a lot
Yes! Very engaging and knowledgeable professor
Absolutely! Great professor and great class.
Yes. I have thoroughly enjoyed Don Moore's expertise and we are lucky to have the opportunity to grow a relationship with him and continue learning from him!
A lot of energy, incentivizes a lot of participation from students. I lacked a bit of application advice or toolkit because the content is very relevant in business and personal settings.
Yes, it is interesting. However, right now it doesn't seem very useful but I have a feeling that maybe in the future it will be...
Yes absolutely. Be ready to challenge yourself and your classmates biases. Don Moore is an absolute treasure. Yes, great content

This class was really interesting and should be taken by anyone who has never been a leader or who thinks they're a really good leader already, because it challenges certain assumptions we have about how to be an effective leader. Lots of reading required though.

Yes

sections.notFor: People from modern, well-run organizations who find the material repetitive and obvious; one student says it is 'too theoretical' and would not recommend.
sections.workloadNote: Not quantified. Structure is in-class activities/exercises, guided discussion, a 1:1 component and research-based content over a compressed 7 weeks.
sections.gradingBasis: unclear
sections.redFlags: One says Moore is rusty after his deanship; one reports he cuts people off and 'sets up logical traps' students fall into; 3 call the material obvious, repetitive or too theoretical.
sections.quote: So I would recommend it to someone who hasn't engaged with the material before, or is coming from a poorly run organization. Frankly, a lot of the material felt repetitive and obvious to me

Not recommended

Out of all the classes I have taken thus far, it will be the lessons and stories I learned in leading people that stick with me.

Yes - I found it extremely insightful to learn about the different leadership successes and pitfalls
Yes, it helped me to challenge my own thoughts
Yes, every business student needs core leadership learning, this format was well organized and linked to careers Yes, don is awesome.
Yes I would. Don gives great material in class and during 1:1 for us to learn.

Yes - if you come to class with an open mind, apply critical thinking, and proactively participate - this class can be very powerful. This is definitely a course where you get what you put into it and classmates being mutually engaged can make the class even more meaningful.
Yes. Leadership is so important and I wish we had this for Fall B too

Strongly recommend fellow student to take this course. Coming to this course, I know that I have a lot leadership areas that I need to improve. This class has helped me define my growth areas and challenged some of the leadership mindset I had developed before whether consciously or unconsciously.
Yes!! I think that it did a good job of teaching the foundations of leadership

This professor is well intentioned and willing to adapt. He is extremely knowledgeable, and adds useful in-class exercises. Will definitely recommend - this course establishes grounds to implement defining leadership principles regularly and instrumentally

Yes. Very engaging. Very grounded in evidence. Lots of myths were brought down for me. I believe I can now operationalize leadership, instead of having the perception it just depends on innate traits.

sections.goodFor: Students interested in consulting or the nonprofit/social sector who want a real client engagement and are prepared for a heavy, self-directed lift as a team lead.
sections.notFor: Anyone expecting structured support or teaching - two of four say team leads get no guidance, team members are overwhelmed, and the course material gives no direction on execution.
sections.workloadNote: Described as 'a lot of work, particularly for team leads', driven entirely by the client consulting project. Only 4 comments - evidence is very thin.
sections.gradingBasis: Client presentations graded as they are delivered live to the client, which one student calls unfair.
sections.redFlags: 2 of 4 raise serious issues: no training or structured communication for team leads, presentations graded live in front of paying clients with no polish round, course material called useless.
sections.quote: It's like teaching someone to drive a train while you're also building the tracks. There isn't the necessary support or guidance for team leads
comments: 0/10 would recommend. I don't think it felt like a worthwhile use of time and I'm not sure what I was supposed to take away from this. I just think the entire premise of this course is flawed.

It's like teaching someone to drive a train while you're also building the tracks. There isn't the necessary support or guidance for team leads and team members get overwhelmed without any prior expertise in the field. There needs to be more structured communication to the team leads ahead of time and throughout the course. Also, it doesn't make any sense to grade presentations as it is being delivered to the client - we should get graded on a run through and then have the opportunity to polish and improve for the actual client presentation. I am actually shocked that these clients pay $25k for students who don't know what they're doing. And finally, the course material is kind of useless. It doesn't actually provide any direction about how to execute these projects.
Great course! Highly recommend to folks who are interested in consulting but be warned it is a lot of work, particularly for team leads.
Yes, if you are interested in the nonprofit space

sections.notFor: Anyone without bandwidth for heavy hours, especially as Team Lead. One student was frustrated at acting as a university ambassador at pre/post receptions — it 'can feel icky.'
sections.workloadNote: Very thin evidence (4 comments). Consistently flagged as a lot of work, especially for Team Leads, with hours ballooning when teammates underperform. Semester-long client engagement.
sections.gradingBasis: Real client consulting project with McKinsey coach support; grading not discussed.
sections.redFlags: With only 4 comments: instructor described as 'competent but not remarkable'; hours spike badly when the team struggles; the ambassador/reception obligations felt uncomfortable to one student.
sections.quote: Just brace yourself for a lot of work, especially if you are a Team Lead

3. Just brace yourself for a lot of work, especially if you are a Team Lead

The course, absolutely yes. Instructor was competent but not remarkable. If you're trying to go into the impact space, this is a fantastic opportunity to work with a client on an interesting problem. Client work is messy, and it's important to have this experience if it's of interest to you. 3 people that I know segued this opportunity into a summer internship, which is a huge plus. Make sure you are selective with your topic and the work it entails--I learned a TONNNNN about something completely new in an area I found fascinating. Also VERY dependent on your team, mine was incredible but at points where the team struggled, I was picking up a lot of the slack and it added immense amount of hours. I was frustrated with the pre- and post-receptions--you're very much working for the university as an ambassador for future work, and if that's something you're not comfortable with it can feel icky.
Yes I would. Although the class was really challenging, I feel like it mimicked what I might encounter working in the social sector and gave me an opportunity to step up as a team lead.

sections.goodFor: Commenters say virtually every MBA should take it: practical, science-backed frameworks for navigating power, influence, networks, and office politics in any career, with self-reflection many found genuinely enlightening. The flipped-classroom, experiential format and Brandi's energy drew repeated praise.
sections.notFor: One commenter would only recommend the course if taught by a different professor; otherwise no one warned students off.
sections.workloadNote: Described as just right and not overly burdensome; not too hard, but built around activities and self-reflection.
sections.quote: Power and politics was arguably the most valuable course I took at Haas. It taught me a lot about myself, and more importantly, how others perceive me.

sections.goodFor: Repeatedly called one of the best classes at Haas for anyone targeting VC or planning to raise from VCs as a founder; the guest speaker lineup (managing partners across stages and sectors) is cited as worth the class by itself. Works for true beginners and experienced VC folks alike, per multiple commenters.
sections.notFor: Despite the title there is essentially no private equity or LBO content, so skip it if PE is your goal. Several students without a finance or VC background felt lost when lectures jumped into calculations, and those wanting deep technical valuation training or casual observers unwilling to carry the heavy, participation-driven load were disappointed.
sections.workloadNote: Heavier than a typical MBA elective: a case per class, substantial reading, and assignments several called hard, though most felt the work translated directly into learning.
sections.gradingBasis: Participation weighs heavily (one student cites 35% of the final grade), with case discussions, cold calling, problem sets, and a venture team component.
sections.redFlags: Recurring (5+ comments): no PE content despite the course name; recurring (4+ comments): assumes VC/finance background and newcomers can feel lost; a few (3): cold-calling and participation pressure felt excessive; isolated: outdated cases from the 90s/2000s, assignments disconnected from class.
sections.quote: Yes, this class was extremely worthwhile. If you want to learn about venture capital this class is a must. One of the best classes offered in the entire MBA program.

comments: Absolutely - specially if you're interested in getting real life experience more about impact and climate investing and/or working with it.

I learned a lot with this course, but I think part of it was because of the client we were assigned to. Potentially this is a class that the more you give the more you get, and part of it depends on the clients engagement and organization to support the project.

Amazing opportunity to connect with the impact and climate investing space - we got to know a lot of the clients and part of them (not only ours) joined the final happy hour and we were able to network more.
Yes, this was a fantastic class for anyone that wants hands-on experience in impact investing

Yes if you're interested in hands-on experience in impact investing. Both instructors are very willing to share their expertise and time with you, the lectures themselves are very informative, and I highly recommend this class.
Yes
Definitely would recommend the course! I thought this was a great experience working with a client and learning real world applications of what we learn in the classroom.
Yes, especially for future investors! It's fun and meaningful to work with real VCs/investors.
Yes if you already have experience in this industry. If you are new it is how much you put into this class.

A lot of our project felt self-driven, and we kind of lost the benefit of working with someone who works in the industry- we didn't really get to know what he does on a day-to-day basis. Yes! Your experience will be somewhat colored by the client youre paired with but regardless, the class is an incredible value add. You'll also have a lot of opportunities to learn from your classmates' projects.

This class is entirely based on your client project, with little to no lecture or deep learning coming from the professors. In fact, class is often cancelled (at the last minute) to give us more "project work time." Honestly, I was hoping to learn more about impact investing from the professors who are such seasoned professionals in this space, but they seem to believe that it's only worthwhile to learn by doing through our client projects, which are highly variable depending on the assigned client and topic.

This was a fantastic class! We had the chance to work with real-world clients and could select them during the first week. I really appreciated how dedicated Etter and Liz were to our growth and supporting us throughout the process. Coming in with no understanding of impact investing (or investing, in general), I felt like it helped to provide me with a deeper understanding and real-world skills.

If you want to work in VC, TAKE THIS CLASS! As someone who is looking to pivot into Climate VC, this may have been the single most impactful class I took in my first year at Haas. Landing a first role in venture is hard, but this class gives you the practical experience to make it easier. The connections with your client are also very helpful, and mine led to an in-semester internship with a fund my client connected me with.
I would recommend this class as it does a great job of tying in the real world into Haas. It was also extremely interesting to see all the other projects other teams were covering.

Good class, very hands-on, but like any applied innovation, the workload and overall class experience depends heavily on the group and client you are assigned. I feel like the class can end up being a lot of work for only 2 units if you don't set a clear scope with your client or get a hard to tackle problem. A lot of the class is self-driven and learning is meant to be peer-to-peer, so this might not be the best class if you are looking for an introductory overview of the impact investing space.
Absolutely, fantastic instructors that bring deep industry knowledge and a great network
Yes fun class and engaging

I would definitely recommend this course if you are interested in climate investing. The projects themselves vary, but Liz and Etter are great resources if you are willing to engage with the class and put in the time.
Yes I would especially if you have never thought about impact investing (applications, capital structures etc.)

sections.goodFor: Students wanting foundations in climate change and how companies are acting on it - including where companies mislead people about their actions.

yes

Climate change is foundational for all future business leaders and for any students that would like to learn foundations, this is a great course to take. The classes can feel long if the topic is not one you're interested in but overall the course encapsulates a lot over the semester.

sections.goodFor: Students in any function (design, engineering, marketing, business) who want hands-on customer discovery and user-need research through real conversations outside school.

Ofcourse! This was a great experience overall. I would prefer a bit more structure and guidance. Your experience solely depends on your team dynamic and you pretty much have to do everything on your own. There are no individual assignments, just presentations to update on progress, so some team members tend to slack and this can be quite frustrating and discouraging. As long as you are willing to give it your all, you will have a good experience. The entire class spins around the business model canvas, so if that is something you are interested in, go for it. If not, take the weekend starup dsico. I took both and startup disco pretty much teaches you all the necessary skill sets. Yes, good experience talking to people outside of school and haven't had any interaction with
Yes- both were great. It has been the best course I've taken so far.
Yes, because it is a course where you learn through experience.
I would but I would make sure to tell the students to be intentional with the project selections; it should mean something to them and really make them curious.
I would recommend this to other students because doing customer discovery and understanding user need is the most important part of any business. Regardless of what role you work.
Yes I would recommend very unique and in depth perspectives

Yes, in this class you can learn the basic structure of the business model and let you know how an early-stage startup needs to approach when they are trying to find their customers' needs. But you need to be familiar with the resources and choose an ideal topic, or you may not gain the result you want. Besides, the whole process is to some degree iterative.

sections.goodFor: Students who want hands-on design-thinking and innovation tools, a consultant-for-a-week experience, and an international/cultural break from normal Haas classes.
sections.notFor: Introverts who find high-intensity workshops overstimulating (1 explicit), and anyone who needs structure or expects a polished final idea out of one week.

comments: Yes. Great course with real experience
Yes. THNK particularly. Rod and Alyssa are very well experienced and it felt eased to do the practices under their guidance in class.

Yes. If you are looking for an opportunity to learn design thinking, improve your knowledge of it and explore different tools, this is the right class for you. I loved that we built and tested a prototype all in one week.
I highly recommend applying for this hands-on course. The class is very diverse. Content is will structured and applicable.
100% recommend this course! It was a great way to get out of the usual day-to-day of Haas. It exposed me to new ideas, new places, and new people - basically, what Haas is all about.
Yes! It was fun, professional and organized - a good balance from real world experiences, educational and also experience a foreign culture!
Absolutely give this course a try if you are looking for inspiration to lead change through innovation. The frameworks are super helpful to implement in any function.

I would definitely recommend this class! The THNK school is amazing and I loved our topic and how it was related to sustainability and consumer products. The THNK school provided us with experiences and tools to explore many new concepts and ideas. This class also got me super excited about exploring entrepreneurship (although not directly related to it), so happy with my decision to take the class!
Yes - it was a great course. One of my favorite experiences of my time at Haas.

It's a decent class to take to get a new perspective on how to innovate and have design thinking to problem solving. It's scrappy and workshoppy and expect very little structure and a way of trying things and failing fast. Worthwhile. The class is highly engaging and can be overstimulating for some introverts, but a great introduction on innovation. Safe and fun environment to pilot innovation concepts.
Along with Embodied Leadership is the course that I've got out the most during Haas.
High value course. Don't miss. Tons of frameworks and insights to be learned in a practical way. An opportunity to experience being a consultant for a week and apply all the learnings.
I would highly recommend this course. It's a great real world application of innovation principles.
Absolutely recommend this course! Sam is a fantastic instructor and the THNK team is great. Highly interactive project-based course.

This is a valuable course if you're interested in real innovation techniques and tools. You need to adjust your expectations that your final product idea will be the best idea you've ever had — impossible in one week — but if you're in it for the process then this is a great way to learn and do in real time for a real client and real problem. The instructor Sam has great innovation industry experience and has curated this class so intentionally and in a way that will help MBA students to think differently about what the true value of design-thinking and consulting services should be.

sections.goodFor: Students who want an intense, hands-on design-thinking and idea-generation experience abroad, and who like being pushed out of their comfort zone with real city/AI stakeholders.
sections.notFor: People wanting a directly transferable skill - one says design thinking doesn't suit every org or role. Leadership games can frustrate, and the immersive format brings real highs and lows.

comments: Yes, good immersive experience on real-world project
If you want o see your ideas come to fruition in small and fast paced manner, while enjoying those small wins, this class is a perfect blend of theories and practice.
Yes!! Sam was an excellent instructor

Yes, this course is very experiential and impactful but if please bring your full self without distractions as this can make a real difference in your mental models. While everyday being in Amsterdam may look fun, use the daily reflections properly to carry forward the learnings long term.

The class teaches a fascinating way to focus on the idea generation and user need. Often, we are focused soley on creating solutions at work from a problem statement. It's rare to spend a bulk of the time actually going through the motions of asking questions, thinking about user needs, and coming to form ideas rather than trying to nail a problem. Yes absolutely! Sam makes learning fun! He shared innovation concepts through understandable and memorable exercises that I'll be able to use in my daily work moving forward!
I would recommend this course for someone with prior consulting experience as a lot of teams had consultants and it put them at an advantage. There is also favoritism so be mindful of that.

Yes, I would wholeheartedly recommend this course. It was an awesome way to push me out of my comfort zone and force me to focus on listening to needs and ideating rather than jumping to solutions which is something I love to do. I got to hands on vibe code which is valuable and fun. I also was forced to constantly think about more roles on teams and how to step back and let other ideas shine. I love the week long immersive course format, there is so much excitement and so much to learn when that's all that occupies your mind. It was also such a valuable way to understand other cultures through the lens of innovation and business. I don't know when I will have the opportunity to do something like this again. On the downsides be prepare to play a lot of leadership games (that sometimes can feel frustrated), constantly feel like you don't have enough time, and expect the highs and lows of an immersive experience like this one. Overall this class pushed me most out of my comfort zone of any class at Haas and really shakes up the traditional format for classes which is so fun.
I would definitely recommend the course. The ability to learn about leadership and innovation in practice in a new environment is very unique

Yes! Great week in Amsterdam. The THNK school is sort of like an IDEO, where you get to work on a case study and go through the full discovery to prototyping process. The stakeholders (in our case, the city of Amsterdam and AI professionals) were great! And the THNK staff (shout out to Edna who coordinated our great lunches) were super accommodating and personable. Fun design sprint, and useful whether you are a novice or familiar.
Yes
Yes; this was a fun, fast-paced course that was really focused on applied learning and different than any other classes I've taken at Haas.
Yes

Yes I would recommend Sam, I wish he taught some other courses because he brings a lot of fun and practical application to the course, which is sometimes lacking in other courses. You will gets hands on in his class and he will push you to improve and experiment in an enjoyable way.

Here you learned design thinking process, this is cool process but it's not suitable for every role and org. So to consider that before applying if you're truly want something practical it might not for you. But if you want a fun experience in Amsterdam this course can give you exactly that.
Yes. This is a very fun and educational experience. Being hands on in a meaningful project is all business graduates need to grow and work with a diverse group of people.
Yes, I would recommend Sam! He was a wonderful instructor.
Course would be better if there's increased fluidity to the exercises
Yes absolutely
